title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
福建武舉錄序
文武並設制科非有重輕也
今年八月福建開文科論薦
文士當是時八郡之士雲集
巡按御史胡志夔加意規畫
而復謀諸百執事曰士所以
三試貴其究經術識治體通
===
今博古具衆長也予聞分經
校閱善矣然專於一人恐其
有所偏不足以得兼長之士
於是以三試卷更三人校之
三人合然後聚而訂之而拔
其尤者故九十人者皆篤志
力學蚤有聲於鄉黨庠序者
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄前序　一
punctuated:
福建武舉錄序

文武並設制科，非有重輕也。

今年八月，福建開文科，論薦文士。當是時，八郡之士雲集。巡按御史胡志夔加意規畫，而復謀諸百執事曰：「士所以三試，貴其究經術、識治體、通今博古、具衆長也。予聞分經校閱，善矣，然專於一人，恐其有所偏，不足以得兼長之士。」於是以三試卷更三人校之，三人合，然後聚而訂之，而拔其尤者。故九十人者，皆篤志力學、蚤有聲於鄉黨庠序者
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Military Provincial Examination

Regular examinations have been established for both civil and military candidates; neither is accorded greater or lesser weight.

In the eighth month of this year, Fujian held the civil examination to assess and recommend civil scholars. At that time, scholars from the eight prefectures gathered like clouds. The Regional Inspector, Censor Hu Zhikui, took particular care in planning the arrangements and further consulted the assembled officials, saying: “The reason scholars undergo three examination sessions is that we prize thorough learning in the Classics, an understanding of the essentials of governance, knowledge of the present and broad acquaintance with antiquity, and the possession of many strengths. I have heard that papers are assigned for assessment according to the Classic treated. This is good; yet if assessment rests exclusively with one person, I fear that his judgment may be partial and insufficient to identify scholars possessing a combination of strengths.” Accordingly, the papers from the three sessions were passed in turn to three examiners for assessment. Once the three agreed, they met to settle their judgments and selected the most outstanding candidates. Thus the ninety selected were all men of firm resolve and diligent study who had already won reputations in their communities and schools …

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
也十月當武舉御史增餙百
度修於往事先期檄勉學與
叅議吳天壽職提調副使劉
廷誥僉事徐光啓職監試及
期集叅政朱徵副使盧夢陽
都指揮奴管蔣麒觀射于演
武之堂初試騎射御史下令
===
曰予聞投牒乞試士有一人
占二名者欲一不中而再中
其遺甲士衛已射者勿得離
次於是虛占名籍不得迭入
應射者若干人再試步射御
史又下令曰予聞武舉士長
於射而短於藝者陰以人代
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄前序 二
punctuated: 也。十月，當武舉，御史增餙百度，修於往事。先期檄勉學與叅議吳天壽職提調，副使劉廷誥、僉事徐光啓職監試。及期，集叅政朱徵、副使盧夢陽、都指揮奴管蔣麒，觀射于演武之堂。初試騎射，御史下令曰：「予聞投牒乞試士，有一人占二名者，欲一不中而再中。其遺甲士衛已射者，勿得離次。」於是虛占名籍，不得迭入。應射者若干人。再試步射，御史又下令曰：「予聞武舉士長於射而短於藝者，陰以人代
translation_en:
…such were they. In the tenth month, when the military examination was held, the Censor enhanced the various procedures, improving upon past practice. Before the appointed date, he issued an official dispatch directing Mianxue and Administration Vice Commissioner Wu Tianshou to serve as Proctors, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Liu Tinggao and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xu Guangqi to supervise the examination. When the day arrived, he assembled Administration Vice Commissioner Zhu Zheng, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Lu Mengyang, and Regional Military Commissioner [Nu Guan?] Jiang Qi to observe the archery at the Hall for Military Exercises.

At the first test, mounted archery, the Censor issued an order: “I have heard that among the men submitting applications to take the examination, some register under two names, hoping that if they fail under one, they may succeed under the other. Let armored soldiers be sent [?] to guard those who have already shot; they must not leave their assigned places.” Thus those fraudulently registered under additional names could not enter repeatedly. A certain number of men presented themselves for the archery test.

At the second test, archery on foot, the Censor again issued an order: “I have heard that military examination candidates who excel at archery but are deficient in literary composition secretly have others substitute for them…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
之無所佐驗其核合射式者
面書狀於是劣於藝者度不
得免不赴步射又若干人一
轉移之間剗除厳習人以此
服御史之高識長慮經文緯
武蓋前所未睹云及三試綜
理校閱一如文舉之舊取中
===
式者得二十七人張鷹揚宴
盛供具歌兎罝采薇以賞多
士而副使姚一元初至共觀
其盛故事刻其名氏與文爲
録勉學以職事承御史之命
爲序人言太平日輕武重文
此爲論者過也
banxin: 武舉鄉試録前序 三
punctuated:
之，無所佐驗，其核合射式者面書狀。」於是劣於藝者度不得免，不赴步射，又若干人。一轉移之間，剗除厳習，人以此服御史之高識長慮，經文緯武，蓋前所未睹云。及三試，綜理校閱，一如文舉之舊，取中式者得二十七人。張鷹揚宴，盛供具，歌《兎罝》《采薇》，以賞多士。而副使姚一元初至，共觀其盛。故事，刻其名氏與文爲録。勉學以職事承御史之命爲序。
人言太平日輕武重文，此爲論者過也。
translation_en:
…in their place, with no supporting means of verification. Let those verified as meeting the archery requirements write a declaration in person.” Consequently, a further number of men deficient in literary composition, judging that they could not escape detection, did not attend the foot archery test. With a single adjustment, pernicious practices [?] were swept away. People thus admired the Censor’s keen discernment and foresight: such coordination of civil and military affairs had apparently never been seen before. At the third test, all administration and assessment followed the established procedures of the civil examination. Twenty-seven men passed. An Eagle-Soaring Banquet was held, with lavish provisions, and “The Rabbit Net” (Tu ju) and “Gathering Ferns” (Cai wei) were sung to reward the candidates. Deputy Commissioner Yao Yiyuan, who had just arrived, joined in witnessing the splendid occasion. Following precedent, the successful candidates’ names and compositions were engraved for publication as a record. I, Mianxue, acting in my official capacity, received the Censor’s command to write this preface.
People say that in times of peace military affairs are slighted and civil affairs esteemed. Those who make this argument are mistaken.

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
聖祖以武功定天下置五府總軍
旅位諸卿上在外置都指揮
使品級亦在藩臬之上
列聖承之不少變
祖宗之制實重武也今夫文吏以
起家進士爲最顯其能致位
卿相者積數十年勤勞經歷
艱難無毫髮玷缺而後可得
===
卽蒙
恩錄廕止於其子雖大有功於民
弗侯也稍畔禮法則沒齒擯
棄蓋自古以文法繩檢文吏
大抵詳密不獨今日也夫以
武功顯者如彼搴旗奪將摧
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄前序 四
punctuated:
聖祖以武功定天下，置五府總軍旅，位諸卿上；在外置都指揮使，品級亦在藩臬之上。列聖承之，不少變。祖宗之制，實重武也。
今夫文吏以起家進士爲最顯，其能致位卿相者，積數十年勤勞，經歷艱難，無毫髮玷缺，而後可得。卽蒙恩錄廕，止於其子；雖大有功於民，弗侯也。稍畔禮法，則沒齒擯棄。蓋自古以文法繩檢文吏，大抵詳密，不獨今日也。夫以武功顯者，如彼搴旗奪將，摧
translation_en:
The sagely founder pacified All under Heaven through military achievement. He established the Five Chief Military Commissions to command the armed forces, ranking them above the chief ministers. Outside the capital, he established Regional Military Commissioners, whose ranks likewise stood above those of the provincial administration and surveillance officials. Successive sage emperors maintained these arrangements without the slightest change. The ancestral institutions indeed accorded great weight to military service.
Now, among civil officials, entering official life as a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) is considered the most distinguished beginning. Those who attain the positions of chief minister or grand councillor can do so only after accumulating decades of diligent service, enduring hardships, and remaining free of the slightest blemish or fault. Even if granted the favor of hereditary privilege, it extends only to their sons; however great their service to the people, they are not made marquises. If they deviate even slightly from ritual propriety and law, they are excluded from office for the rest of their lives. Since antiquity, the statutory rules used to regulate civil officials have generally been detailed and exacting; this is not peculiar to the present day. As for those distinguished by military achievement, such as those who seize enemy banners, capture enemy commanders, and break…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
鋒萬里開拓疆宇樹大勲勞
固當世食其報而其他俘斬
獻馘自一級而上並得叙錄
功收於一戰百世子孫食報
無盡也又待之以疏節卽遭
裁抑不絶其祿已廢復起由
此觀之孰輕孰重彰明較著
===
矣曩歲以武舉不得人有
詔停罷尋復舉行間者倭夷不靖
煽禍吳越閩爲唇齒亦切隄
備需將材甚急故今年武舉
御史益加意其所張設夸耀
以示奬勸赫然與文舉較勝
爭隆也
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄前序　五
punctuated:
鋒萬里，開拓疆宇，樹大勲勞，固當世食其報。而其他俘斬獻馘，自一級而上，並得叙錄，功收於一戰，百世子孫食報無盡也。又待之以疏節，卽遭裁抑，不絶其祿；已廢復起。由此觀之，孰輕孰重，彰明較著矣。
曩歲以武舉不得人，有詔停罷，尋復舉行。間者倭夷不靖，煽禍吳越，閩爲唇齒，亦切隄備，需將材甚急。故今年武舉，御史益加意，其所張設夸耀，以示奬勸，赫然與文舉較勝爭隆也。
translation_en:
…enemy ranks over ten thousand li, extending the realm’s borders and establishing great achievements: such men certainly deserve to enjoy their rewards generation after generation. Yet others who take captives, kill enemies, and present severed ears as proof receive recognition and registration of their merit for as little as a single enemy head. Merit is won in one battle, while descendants for a hundred generations enjoy its rewards without end. Moreover, they are treated with less exacting formal requirements. Even when subjected to restrictions or demotion, their stipends are not cut off; once dismissed, they are appointed again. Viewed in this light, which is treated lightly and which accorded weight is abundantly clear.
In former years, because the military examinations failed to obtain suitable men, an imperial edict suspended them; before long, they were held again. Recently, Japanese raiders have caused unrest, spreading disaster through Wu and Yue. Fujian, linked to those regions as lips are to teeth, likewise urgently needs defensive preparations, and its need for talented commanders is acute. Thus, for this year’s military examination, the Censor has taken still greater care. The arrangements and splendid displays intended to encourage and reward candidates conspicuously rival the civil examination in magnificence and distinction.

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
皇上痛念東南腹心之患博采廷
議
特命重臣提兵致討時則工部侍
郎趙文華屢獻嘉猷爲
上所眷知授以督察軍務之任而
實假之以招來豪俊之權兵
部侍郎楊宜則以臺省崇望
===
負文武之具特受
節鉞爲之總制都御史胡宗憲則
以風裁振肅奏破賊之功特
承
殊簡爲之督撫彼三重臣者矢心
戮力期旦夕滅虜獻俘苟有
一節之士可備任使徵書絡
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄前序　六
punctuated: 皇上痛念東南腹心之患，博采廷議，特命重臣提兵致討。時則工部侍郎趙文華屢獻嘉猷，爲上所眷知，授以督察軍務之任，而實假之以招來豪俊之權。兵部侍郎楊宜則以臺省崇望，負文武之具，特受節鉞，爲之總制。都御史胡宗憲則以風裁振肅，奏破賊之功，特承殊簡，爲之督撫。彼三重臣者，矢心戮力，期旦夕滅虜獻俘。苟有一節之士可備任使，徵書絡
translation_en: His Majesty, deeply troubled by the affliction threatening the vital heartland of the southeast, widely sought deliberations at court and specially ordered high ministers to lead troops in a punitive campaign. At this time, Zhao Wenhua, Vice Minister of Works, repeatedly offered sound counsel and enjoyed the emperor’s favor and recognition. He was entrusted with supervising military affairs and, in effect, granted authority to recruit outstanding men. Yang Yi, Vice Minister of War, enjoyed great prestige in the censorial and central administrative offices and possessed both civil and military abilities. He was specially invested with the tally and battle-axe of command to serve as Supreme Commander. Hu Zongxian, Censor-in-Chief, inspired awe and discipline through his bearing and judgment and reported successes in defeating the bandits. By special imperial selection, he was appointed to oversee military affairs and serve as Grand Coordinator. These three high ministers pledged themselves wholeheartedly and joined their efforts, hoping to destroy the marauders and present captives at court within days. If there was any man with even one worthy quality who could be employed, letters summoning him came in a stream…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
繹不絕夫豈愛吐哺握髮交
章綴牘哉都御史汪尚寧控
扼四省之衝嚴固保障以防
竊發亦未嘗一日不以求將
爲念也諸士懐材抱略正入
彀脫頴之日嘗聞之君子所
貴在排難解紛立身揚名昔
===
曾子以戰陳無勇爲非孝蓋
戰陳不勇則名不揚名不揚
則親不顯孰謂全軀滅名得
爲孝子哉嘗讀史記凡所稱
述驍勇囊智之士有軍功者
則其辭愈悲壯激烈附見於
本紀特見於世家列傳者不
banxin: 武舉鄉試録前序 七
punctuated:
繹不絕，夫豈愛吐哺握髮、交章綴牘哉？都御史汪尚寧控扼四省之衝，嚴固保障，以防竊發，亦未嘗一日不以求將爲念也。

諸士懐材抱略，正入彀脫頴之日。嘗聞之，君子所貴在排難解紛，立身揚名。昔曾子以戰陳無勇爲非孝，蓋戰陳不勇則名不揚，名不揚則親不顯，孰謂全軀滅名得爲孝子哉？嘗讀《史記》，凡所稱述驍勇囊智之士，有軍功者，則其辭愈悲壯激烈。附見於本紀、特見於世家列傳者，不
translation_en:
… continued in an unbroken stream. How could they begrudge spitting out their food or grasping their unbound hair to receive worthy men, or submitting memorial after memorial and composing document after document? Censor-in-chief Wang Shangning controls the strategic crossroads of four provinces, strengthening their defenses against sudden outbreaks of rebellion. Not a day has passed without his giving thought to finding commanders.

You gentlemen possess talent and strategic understanding: this is precisely the time to enter the ranks of those selected and let your abilities stand out. I have heard that what the gentleman prizes is resolving difficulties and disputes, establishing himself, and making his name illustrious. In antiquity, Zengzi regarded a lack of courage in battle as unfilial. For without courage in battle, one’s name does not become illustrious; without an illustrious name, one’s parents receive no distinction. Who could say that preserving one’s body while extinguishing one’s reputation makes one a filial son? I have read the Records of the Grand Historian. Among the men of valor and resourcefulness [?] whom it celebrates, those with military achievements are described in language still more stirring, impassioned, and heroic. Those mentioned incidentally in the Basic Annals or given particular notice in the Hereditary Houses and Biographies cannot …

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
可勝道他如恩加於百姓者
傳之循吏功究於詩書者傳
之儒林無乃數人耳是文吏
修職勤業積以歲年而不見
稱述者何限也孰與武夫收
功於一戰名聞當時聲施後
世與載籍同永久哉夫服絺
===
綌之凉者不畏炎暑之鬱燠
襲狐貉之煖者不憂至寒之
悽愴何者有其具者易其備
也順風而呼聲不加疾而聞
者遠登山而招臂不加長而
見者衆有所乗故也千金之
裘非一狐之腋大厦之材非
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄前序　八
punctuated:
可勝道。他如恩加於百姓者，傳之循吏；功究於詩書者，傳之儒林，無乃數人耳。是文吏修職勤業，積以歲年，而不見稱述者何限也！孰與武夫收功於一戰，名聞當時，聲施後世，與載籍同永久哉？
夫服絺綌之凉者，不畏炎暑之鬱燠；襲狐貉之煖者，不憂至寒之悽愴。何者？有其具者，易其備也。順風而呼，聲不加疾而聞者遠；登山而招，臂不加長而見者衆，有所乗故也。千金之裘，非一狐之腋；大厦之材，非
translation_en:
…too numerous to recount. Others, such as those whose beneficence reached the common people, are recorded in the biographies of upright officials; those whose scholarly achievements extended to the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents are recorded in the biographies of Confucian scholars. Are these not merely a handful? How countless, then, are the civil officials who diligently fulfilled their duties and pursued their work year after year, yet received no praise or record! How could they compare with warriors who achieve merit in a single battle, whose names become known in their own time and whose fame spreads to later generations, enduring as long as the written records themselves?
Those who wear cool garments of fine or coarse ramie do not fear the oppressive heat of summer; those clad in warm fox and raccoon-dog furs do not worry about the misery of extreme cold. Why is this? Those who possess the requisite means can readily make their preparations. Call with the wind at your back: your voice is no louder, yet people hear it farther away. Climb a mountain and wave: your arm is no longer, yet more people see it. This is because there is something to take advantage of. A fur robe worth a thousand pieces of gold does not come from the underarm fur of a single fox; the timber for a great mansion does not come from…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
一丘之木則共濟之力也協
共濟之力乘可爲之勢而出
其有爲之具則何患乎功業
之不建而名號長美也多士
之來蓋爲名也故以立身揚
名之說爲多士勗焉是舉也
監察御史吉澄奉
===
命代巡初辭
闕下風聲所被士氣丕振右布
政使楊應奇僉事吳朝鳳署
都指揮僉事王夢麒來熙則
先期入
賀按察使趙維垣則先期入
覲僉事袁洪愈王宗聖叅將尹
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄前序 九
punctuated:
一丘之木，則共濟之力也。協共濟之力，乘可爲之勢，而出其有爲之具，則何患乎功業之不建而名號長美也？多士之來，蓋爲名也，故以立身揚名之說爲多士勗焉。
是舉也，監察御史吉澄奉命代巡，初辭闕下，風聲所被，士氣丕振。右布政使楊應奇、僉事吳朝鳳、署都指揮僉事王夢麒、來熙則先期入賀，按察使趙維垣則先期入覲，僉事袁洪愈、王宗聖、叅將尹
translation_en:
…timber from a single hill: this is the power of joint effort. By combining the strength of joint effort, taking advantage of favorable circumstances, and bringing forth the means for accomplishment, what fear need there be that achievements will not be established and names will not enjoy lasting renown [?]? The many candidates have come, surely, to win a name; therefore I offer these words on establishing oneself and making one’s name known as encouragement to them.
For this examination, Investigating Censor Ji Cheng received the imperial command to undertake an inspection tour. He had only just departed from the imperial court when his reputation, wherever it reached, greatly invigorated the spirit of the candidates. Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Yang Yingqi, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wu Chaofeng, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Wang Mengqi and Lai Xi had gone to court beforehand to offer congratulations. Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Zhao Weiyuan had gone to court beforehand for an imperial audience. Surveillance Vice Commissioners Yuan Hongyu and Wang Zongsheng, and Assistant Regional Commander Yin…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
鳳署都指揮僉事黃鎮張漢

text:

本月二十三日題，奉武宗皇帝聖旨：「是。這武舉鄉試條格，都依擬行，便行與南京及在外各該衙門知道。」欽此。
今照兵部侍郎爲本兵之佐，旣知武
translation_en:
…shall set the questions; outside the capitals, the Regional Inspectors shall all set the questions. The policy questions may draw on ancient military methods or address current affairs. They should be concise and contain implications through which the candidates’ abilities and discernment can be assessed. They need not rely exclusively on conventional statements found on paper, rewarding mere memorization and thereby overlooking genuine talent. Those who were previously sent to the Ministry to take the joint examination but failed, and who now present themselves again, shall be permitted to undergo examination and be forwarded on the same terms. Selection shall comprise five grades, following throughout the procedures of the Military Metropolitan Examination. The guards and battalions in the two capitals shall recommend and forward candidates, and the respective Chief Military Commissions shall assemble and forward them to the Central Chief Military Commission. The Upper Ten Guards and the military school shall recommend and forward candidates directly to the Central Chief Military Commission. For each candidate recommended by a guard or battalion, a clear statement must be supplied concerning his customary resourcefulness and courage, his training in mounted archery and military methods, and his having never been subjected to judicial sentencing and dispatch for punishment. The same requirements shall apply to those examined and forwarded from the various localities, and to candidates recommended by provincial commissions, prefectures, subprefectures, counties, guards, and battalions outside the capitals.
A memorial was submitted on the twenty-third day of this month, and the following sacred edict of Emperor Wuzong was received: “Approved. Let all these regulations for the Military Provincial Examination be implemented as proposed. Immediately notify Nanjing and all the relevant offices outside the capitals.” Respectfully received.

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
試馬上箭
第貳場
試步下箭
第叁場
策二道
問將者三軍之司命而國威所視以爲重
輕者也三代而下以名將稱者不可一
二數而論爲將者之貴察幾審勢校計
索情者亦不一而足有所謂五勝四機
===
八弊八惡可得而聞歟又謂惟五事足
以盡爲將之道八徵足以盡選將之法
其果然歟我
國家於勛舊之胄肄于成均武弁之子群于
郡庠閭閻之俊收於射藝建制設科文
武並舉固宜真才彙征而折衝足寄也
邇者倭寇陸梁吳浙被毒
聖天子赫然震怒欲一舉而殄薙之而未見有

punctuated:

問：將者，三軍之司命，而國威所視以爲重輕者也。三代而下，以名將稱者不可一二數，而論爲將者之貴察幾審勢、校計索情者，亦不一而足。有所謂五勝、四機、八弊、八惡，可得而聞歟？又謂惟五事足以盡爲將之道，八徵足以盡選將之法，其果然歟？我國家於勛舊之胄肄于成均，武弁之子群于郡庠，閭閻之俊收於射藝，建制設科，文武並舉，固宜真才彙征，而折衝足寄也。邇者倭寇陸梁，吳浙被毒，聖天子赫然震怒，欲一舉而殄薙之，而未見有
translation_en:
First session: mounted archery.
Second session: archery on foot.
Third session: two policy questions.
Question: A commander holds the lives of the armies in his hands, and the prestige of the state depends upon him for its strength or weakness. Since the Three Dynasties, those celebrated as famous commanders have been too numerous to enumerate. Nor have discussions been few concerning the importance, for a commander, of discerning incipient developments, assessing circumstances, comparing plans, and probing the true situation. There are the so-called five means of victory, four critical opportunities, eight defects, and eight evils. May we hear an account of these? It is also said that just five matters suffice to encompass the way of being a commander, and eight tests suffice to encompass the method of selecting commanders. Is this indeed so?
Our state has the descendants of longstanding meritorious families study at the Imperial University, gathers the sons of military officers in prefectural schools, and recruits outstanding men from among the common people through their skill in archery. It has established institutions and examination categories, promoting civil and military talent alike. Surely men of true ability ought therefore to come forward together, and the task of repelling the enemy ought to be safely entrusted to them. Recently, the Japanese pirates have run rampant, and Wu and Zhejiang have suffered their ravages. The sagely Son of Heaven, stirred to mighty wrath, wishes to annihilate them at a single stroke, yet there have not appeared any …

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
豪傑之士雲合響應任事策勳以紓我
皇上南顧之憂者何歟豈承平日久兵法不講
世果無其才歟抑才固隱於人而求之
未得其道歟夫求將之方若宋富弼范
仲淹歐陽脩蘇洵諸人亦嘗論之詳矣
可得而言之歟其於八徵之說固可行
之於今歟茲欲推轂無拊髀之嘆師師
成獻馘之功抑別有其法歟夫諸士學
爲將者也術固其所自審將不易擇也
而方以類求尤其所素諳請明言之固
當轉之於謀帥者焉
===
問傳曰天生五財民幷用之誰能去兵兵是
兵者國之大事而爲將者不可不知也
然秘謀神機呼吸萬變誠有未易窺測
者試卽古法一二與諸士評之步兵依
丘陵易地則用騎自戰其地爲散爲客
務入則專形人而我無形致人而不致
於人者法也故依其險阻解幽州之圍
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　十六
punctuated:
豪傑之士雲合響應，任事策勳，以紓我皇上南顧之憂者，何歟？豈承平日久，兵法不講，世果無其才歟？抑才固隱於人，而求之未得其道歟？夫求將之方，若宋富弼、范仲淹、歐陽脩、蘇洵諸人，亦嘗論之詳矣，可得而言之歟？其於八徵之說，固可行之於今歟？茲欲推轂無拊髀之嘆，師師成獻馘之功，抑別有其法歟？夫諸士學爲將者也，術固其所自審；將不易擇也，而方以類求，尤其所素諳。請明言之，固當轉之於謀帥者焉。

問：傳曰：「天生五財，民幷用之，誰能去兵？」兵是兵者，國之大事，而爲將者不可不知也。然秘謀神機，呼吸萬變，誠有未易窺測者。試卽古法一二，與諸士評之。步兵依丘陵，易地則用騎；自戰其地爲散，爲客務入則專；形人而我無形，致人而不致於人者，法也。故依其險阻，解幽州之圍，
translation_en:
…outstanding men gathering like clouds and responding like an echo, undertaking responsibilities and earning recorded merit, thereby relieving Our Emperor’s anxiety as he looks southward—why have such men not appeared? Has prolonged peace caused the arts of war to fall into neglect, so that the world truly lacks such talent? Or does talent indeed lie hidden among the people, while the proper means of finding it have yet to be attained? As for methods of finding commanders, such men of the Song as Fu Bi, Fan Zhongyan, Ouyang Xiu, and Su Xun discussed them in detail. Can you set out their views? Can the doctrine of the eight tests indeed be applied today? If we now wish to appoint commanders without occasioning the lament of slapping one’s thigh over the lack of worthy men, and have every army achieve victories marked by the presentation of severed enemy ears, is there some other method? You gentlemen are studying to become commanders, and surely have yourselves carefully considered the requisite arts. Commanders are not easily selected; methods of seeking them among men of your own kind should be especially familiar to you. Please explain these matters clearly. Your statements should assuredly be passed on to those charged with finding commanders.

Question: The Commentary says: “Heaven produces the five resources, and the people use them all. Who can dispense with arms?” Warfare[?] is a great affair of state, and those who would be commanders must understand it. Yet secret plans and inspired stratagems undergo countless changes within a single breath; some are indeed difficult to fathom. Let us take one or two ancient principles and discuss them with you gentlemen. Infantry should rely on hills and heights; on level ground, cavalry should be employed. Fighting within one’s own territory makes for dispersal; when campaigning in another’s territory, pressing deep within it brings concentration. Making the enemy reveal his dispositions while keeping one’s own concealed, and making the enemy come to oneself without being drawn to him—these are principles of warfare. Thus, by relying on difficult terrain, the siege of Youzhou was relieved…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:

而定齊南疑本初而掩白馬是數者於

去疑雨水必俟定而涉風逆必堅陣以

依古法奏六出之捷四蹙馬鞍而大破
益兵一卒爲神而克復宗國傳壘降梁
===

俱能制勝然則料敵出奇果非兵法之
所能盡而曰權勿預定變勿先圖與時
遷移應物變化固設策之機歟諸士業

久矣請著之於篇以觀度越之猷
論
善用兵者脩道而保法

善用兵者脩道而保法。
translation_en:
…drawing them onto the plain, he achieved victory at Hao. The one who resisted Wei fully accepted the advice of his administrative aide; the one who subdued Zhao was glad to have departed from the Lord of Guangwu’s plan. One lured Fei Yi out and pacified southern Qi; another sowed doubts in Benchu’s mind and made a surprise attack at Baima. In these instances, victory was certainly achieved by following the principles of warfare. Yet this was not invariably so.
Protracted warfare is not prized; an army must march out under discipline; do not advance uphill to fight; prohibit divination and dispel doubts; when rain swells a river, wait until its waters settle before crossing; when the wind is against you, maintain a firm formation and wait. These, too, are military principles. How, then, did a vigorous campaign against Jing and Chu achieve its success after three years? How were victories reported in six expeditions that did not follow ancient methods? How did four assaults at Ma’an result in a crushing victory? How did adding a single company of soldiers as divine troops [?] enable the recovery of the ancestral state? How did extending siegeworks [?] bring Liang to surrender, and how did an attack into the wind overcome the enemy? All these actions violated the prohibitions of military doctrine, yet all secured victory.
Does this mean that assessing the enemy and devising unexpected moves truly cannot be fully encompassed by military doctrine? And does the saying, “Do not determine expedients in advance or plan adaptations beforehand; shift with the times and change in response to circumstances,” indeed express the essential workings of strategic planning? You gentlemen devote yourselves to military strategy and have long discussed the successes and failures of ancient commanders. Please set out your views in writing, so that we may see your plans for surpassing them.
Discourse
Those skilled in warfare cultivate the Way and maintain military regulations.

第一問

夫將才之難得，蓋自古然矣。非才之難得，良以其人之不易知也。非獨上之人難於知人，而其人亦不易於自知也。何也？天下之事，未有不學而能、不試而効者也。人情之所畏難而不敢爲者，豈非死傷戰鬬之患，匹夫之所輕，而士大夫不忍以其身親之者耶？故雖有天下之大智且勇者，其平居旣不以軍旅之事爲學，卽學之而亦未嘗有所試，其敢稱於人曰：「我善爲陳，我善爲戰」乎？此人之所以不易知，而其人亦不易於自知也。自古未有借才於異代者也。古昔盛王，當治安之日，而不忘危亂之慮，廣收天下之英雄豪傑而尊寵之，使之講
translation_en:
Policy Essay
First Question
Tang Jia
Six hits in mounted archery; four hits in archery on foot.

The difficulty of finding talented generals has indeed existed since antiquity. It is not that talent itself is hard to find; rather, those who possess it are hard to recognize. Not only do those above find it difficult to recognize such men, but these men themselves also find it difficult to know their own abilities. Why is this? In the affairs of the world, no one can become capable without learning, or prove effective without being put to the test. What people fear as difficult and dare not undertake—is it not the peril of death and injury in battle, which common men treat lightly but which scholar-officials cannot bear to face in person? Thus, even a man of exceptional wisdom and courage, if in ordinary life he has never studied military affairs—or, even if he has studied them, has never had an opportunity to put his learning to the test—would he dare tell others, “I am skilled at deploying battle formations; I am skilled at fighting”? This is why such men are difficult to recognize, and why they themselves find it difficult to know their own abilities. Since antiquity, no age has ever been able to borrow talented men from another. The flourishing kings of old, even in times of peace and good order, never forgot to consider the dangers of turmoil. They gathered outstanding men and heroes from throughout the realm, honored and favored them, and had them engage in study…

厭文德也蓋誠見乎將才之難得而綢繆
之具不可不豫也夫國之有名將也猶山
林之有猛獸江河之有蛟龍也不必恣其
吞噬而人自不敢近何者威怵之也合軍
聚衆屈力殫貨以爭一日之勝不生則死
不存則亡而可委之庸人之手乎此春秋
所以譏鄭棄其師也是故將不擇才譬無
異驅伏鷄而搏狸率乳犬而犯虎也古之
===
人善論將者莫若孔子其言曰臨事而懼
好謀而成而勇力不與焉夫敬事好謀豈
易言哉幾有緩急勢有重輕計有正變情
有虛實毫釐之差千里之繆古之人幸而
成不幸而敗者何多也其善言兵法者太
上莫若太公望其次莫若孫武莫若吳起
縱橫之後莫若諸葛亮今其書具在可俯
而窺也其大指要皆不外乎敬事好謀之
一言其曰知勝有五知可以與戰不可以

punctuated:
求武備。彼其所以爲此者，非以邀戰功而厭文德也。蓋誠見乎將才之難得，而綢繆之具不可不豫也。夫國之有名將也，猶山林之有猛獸、江河之有蛟龍也。不必恣其吞噬，而人自不敢近。何者？威怵之也。合軍聚衆，屈力殫貨，以爭一日之勝，不生則死，不存則亡，而可委之庸人之手乎？此《春秋》所以譏鄭棄其師也。是故將不擇才，譬無異驅伏鷄而搏狸，率乳犬而犯虎也。
古之人善論將者，莫若孔子。其言曰：「臨事而懼，好謀而成。」而勇力不與焉。夫敬事好謀，豈易言哉？幾有緩急，勢有重輕，計有正變，情有虛實。毫釐之差，千里之繆。古之人幸而成、不幸而敗者，何多也！其善言兵法者，太上莫若太公望，其次莫若孫武、莫若吳起，縱橫之後莫若諸葛亮。今其書具在，可俯而窺也。其大指要，皆不外乎敬事好謀之一言。其曰：「知勝有五：知可以與戰、不可以
translation_en:
…to study military preparedness. Their purpose in doing this was not to seek military glory and scorn civil virtue. Rather, they truly recognized how difficult it was to find talented commanders, and that the means of preparedness had to be provided in advance. A state’s possession of renowned generals is like the presence of fierce beasts in mountain forests or dragons in rivers. They need not be allowed to devour at will: people will naturally not dare approach. Why? Their might strikes fear into them. When armies are assembled and multitudes gathered, strength exhausted and resources depleted, to contend for victory on a single day—with death the alternative to life, and destruction the alternative to survival—can this be entrusted to mediocre men? This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals censures Zheng for abandoning its army. Thus, failing to select commanders for their ability is no different from driving crouching chickens to fight a wildcat, or leading suckling puppies to attack a tiger.
Among the ancients who discussed generalship well, none surpassed Kongzi. He said: “One who approaches affairs with apprehension, delights in planning, and brings matters to completion.” Physical courage and strength have no part in this statement. Yet how could taking affairs seriously and delighting in planning be easy matters to discuss? Critical junctures differ in urgency; circumstances differ in gravity; plans involve both regular and adaptive methods; actual conditions may be empty or substantial. An error of a hair’s breadth leads to a discrepancy of a thousand li. How many among the ancients succeeded through good fortune or failed through ill fortune! Among those who expounded the methods of warfare well, none in the earliest times surpassed Taigong Wang; next came Sun Wu and Wu Qi; after the age of the strategists of vertical and horizontal alliances, none surpassed Zhuge Liang. Their books are all still extant today, available for us to bend over and examine. Their essential purport never goes beyond the single phrase “take affairs seriously and delight in planning.” One of these works says: “There are five ways to know victory: knowing when one can engage in battle and when one cannot…”

閑馳逐是謂力機夫兵之有機也猶弩之
===

不可不審也曰將有八弊貪而無厭詐而
心怯妬賢而嫉能信讒而好佞料彼不自
料猶豫不自決荒淫於酒色狂言而不禮

能任賢良政不能正刑法富不能濟窮厄
知不能備未形慮不能防微密達不能舉

punctuated: 與戰者勝；識衆寡之用者勝；上下同欲者勝；以虞待不虞者勝；將能而君不御者勝。」故不知勝，則不能制勝，不可不慎也。曰：「兵有四機：三軍之衆，百萬之師，張設輕重，在於一人，是謂氣機；路狹道險，名山大塞，十夫所守，千夫不過，是謂地機；善行間諜，輕兵往來，分散其衆，使其君臣上下相咎，是謂事機；車堅管轄，舟利櫓楫，士習戰陳，馬閑馳逐，是謂力機。」夫兵之有機也，猶弩之有機，執其機而發之，則用力少而就效衆，不可不審也。曰：「將有八弊：貪而無厭，詐而心怯，妬賢而嫉能，信讒而好佞，料彼不自料，猶豫不自決，荒淫於酒色，狂言而不禮。」弊之爲言也，猶病之在身，死亡立至，不可不治也。曰：「將有八惡：謀不能料是非，理不能任賢良，政不能正刑法，富不能濟窮厄，知不能備未形，慮不能防微密，達不能舉所知，敗不能無怨謗。」以小惡爲無傷，則大
translation_en:
…engage in battle will prevail; those who understand how to employ forces large and small will prevail; those whose superiors and subordinates share the same purpose will prevail; those who, prepared themselves, await the unprepared will prevail; those whose generals are capable and whose ruler does not constrain them will prevail.” Thus, without knowing the conditions for victory, one cannot secure victory. This demands caution.

It says: “Warfare has four crucial mechanisms. In a host of three armies, a force of a million men, the weight of its power when deployed rests upon one man: this is the mechanism of morale. Where routes are narrow and roads perilous, at great mountains and major passes, ten men can hold a position that a thousand cannot pass: this is the mechanism of terrain. Skillfully employing spies, sending light troops back and forth, dispersing the enemy’s forces, and making their ruler and ministers, superiors and subordinates, blame one another: this is the mechanism of operations. Chariots with sturdy axle fittings and linchpins, boats with effective oars and paddles, soldiers practiced in battle formations, and horses trained in galloping and pursuit: this is the mechanism of material strength.” Warfare has mechanisms just as a crossbow has a trigger mechanism. Grasp and release the mechanism, and little effort produces great results. This demands careful scrutiny.

It says: “A general has eight failings: insatiable greed; deceitfulness coupled with cowardice; jealousy of the worthy and envy of the capable; belief in slander and fondness for flattery; assessing the enemy without assessing himself; hesitation and inability to decide for himself; dissipation in wine and women; and reckless speech without propriety.” What we call a failing is like a disease in the body: death can follow at once. It must be treated.

It says: “A general has eight faults: in planning, being unable to judge right and wrong; in management, being unable to employ the worthy and good; in government, being unable to set punishments and laws in order; when wealthy, being unable to relieve those in poverty and distress; in understanding, being unable to prepare for what has not yet taken shape; in deliberation, being unable to guard against subtle and hidden dangers; when successful, being unable to recommend those whose abilities he knows; and when defeated, being unable to refrain from resentment and slander.” If small faults are considered harmless, then great…

者不過一二人待以不次之位試以守邊
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄 盂
punctuated: 警急，卽不免有乏材之憂。取天下之易者，莫若宋，而其在當時，則猶有李漢超等五人使備契丹，郭進等四人使備河東，趙賛等五人使備西羗。其他東征西討，未嘗乏人。慶曆、元祐之間，其主非不有道而守成也，而邊患日熾，中國所以奉西北之虜，歲以百萬，不能支持。在廷之臣，未嘗一日不以求將爲念也。老成長慮者，如范仲淹，則有專督管軍臣僚于諸班中搜羅知勇之人，各舉一名，遷轉於邊上任使，將來頗立戰功，明賞舉主之說；富弼，則有近臣及藩鎭大臣於文武官中各舉練習武略、堪任將帥者一二人，召至闕下，量與遷擢，隨其品位任于邊塞，使其磨勵，以觀其能否之說；蘇洵，則有可復武舉而爲之新制，以革其舊弊，因貢士之歲，使兩制各舉其所聞，有司試其可者，而君上親策之，勇而有謀者不過一二人，待以不次之位，試以守邊
translation_en:
…when an emergency arose, there would inevitably be anxiety over a shortage of capable men. No dynasty won the realm more easily than the Song. Yet at that time it still had Li Hanchao and four others assigned to defend against the Khitan, Guo Jin and three others assigned to defend against Hedong, and Zhao Zan and four others assigned to defend against the Western Qiang. Nor was there ever a shortage of men for its other campaigns east and west. Between the Qingli and Yuanyou reign periods, its rulers were by no means lacking in adherence to the Way as they preserved their inherited dominion. Yet troubles on the frontiers grew daily more intense. What the central realm supplied to the barbarians of the northwest amounted to millions each year, a burden it could not sustain. Not a day passed when the ministers at court did not concern themselves with finding generals.

Among those of mature experience and far-reaching foresight, Fan Zhongyan proposed specifically directing officials commanding troops to search the various military units for men of wisdom and courage. Each official should recommend one man, who would then be transferred and employed on the frontier. If these men subsequently achieved notable military successes, their sponsors should be publicly rewarded. Fu Bi proposed that ministers close to the throne and senior regional military authorities each recommend one or two civil or military officials well versed in military strategy and fit to command armies. These men should be summoned to court, granted promotions as appropriate, and assigned to the frontier according to their rank, so that they might hone their abilities and their competence could be assessed. Su Xun proposed restoring the military examinations and establishing new regulations to eliminate their former abuses. In years when candidates were presented to the court, the officials responsible for drafting imperial edicts in the two drafting services should each recommend men whose abilities they had heard of. The responsible authorities should examine suitable candidates, and the sovereign should personally question them on policy. Those possessing both courage and resourcefulness would number no more than one or two; they should be accorded posts outside the regular order of promotion and tested by being entrusted with frontier defense…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
之任之說歐陽脩則有合百人教之而選
一隊將合十隊將教之而選一裨將合十
裨將教之而選一大將之說其爲慮至遠
而爲畫至精也夷考其時未聞有智勇之
人士若孫吳者以赴徵命豈當時諸臣之
言不盡用歟或用而所委托者不得其人
歟或有其人而不果於嚮用歟信乎人不
易知而其人亦不易於自知也
今天下之大海內之富再倍於宋紀綱之肅法
度之嚴十倍於宋
祖宗教養之澤百倍於宋我
皇上修道致治昭賞定罰赫怒整旅以對天下
日夜憂勞思得一賢將而使之不遑暇食
則又非宋家守成之主可同日而論布列
庶位者非無忠義慷忼之士也又非才術
謀慮不若宋人無舉富范歐蘇之說以告
當宁者也邇者倭夷爲患毒流吳越
朝廷搜羅知勇之士不愛尊官厚祿以戡其
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　二十五
punctuated:
之任之說。歐陽脩則有合百人教之而選一隊將，合十隊將教之而選一裨將，合十裨將教之而選一大將之說。其爲慮至遠，而爲畫至精也。夷考其時，未聞有智勇之人士若孫吳者以赴徵命，豈當時諸臣之言不盡用歟？或用而所委托者不得其人歟？或有其人而不果於嚮用歟？信乎，人不易知，而其人亦不易於自知也。
今天下之大，海內之富，再倍於宋；紀綱之肅，法度之嚴，十倍於宋；祖宗教養之澤，百倍於宋。我皇上修道致治，昭賞定罰，赫怒整旅，以對天下，日夜憂勞，思得一賢將而使之，不遑暇食，則又非宋家守成之主可同日而論。布列庶位者，非無忠義慷忼之士也；又非才術謀慮不若宋人，無舉富范歐蘇之說以告當宁者也。邇者倭夷爲患，毒流吳越，朝廷搜羅知勇之士，不愛尊官厚祿，以戡其
translation_en:
…the proposal to give them responsibility for defending the frontier. Ouyang Xiu proposed gathering a hundred men, training them, and selecting one company commander; gathering ten company commanders, training them, and selecting one subordinate general; and gathering ten subordinate generals, training them, and selecting one commanding general. Their thinking was exceptionally far-reaching, and their planning exceptionally precise. Yet upon examining that period, we hear of no men of wisdom and courage like Sun Wu or Wu Qi answering the summons. Could it be that the proposals of those ministers were not fully adopted? Or were they adopted, but responsibility entrusted to the wrong men? Or were suitable men available, but there was no resolve to employ them? Truly, it is difficult to recognize men’s abilities, and difficult for those men themselves to recognize their own.
Today, the extent of the realm and the wealth within the seas are twice those of the Song; the strictness of discipline and the rigor of laws are ten times those of the Song; and the benefits of our imperial ancestors’ instruction and nurture are a hundred times those of the Song. Our Emperor cultivates the Way and achieves good government, makes rewards manifest and punishments definite, and, in majestic wrath, marshals his troops to confront the affairs of the realm. Anxious and laboring day and night, he longs to find one worthy general to employ, scarcely allowing himself leisure to eat. He cannot be spoken of in the same breath as the Song rulers who merely preserved their inherited dominion. Among those occupying the many offices, there is no lack of loyal, righteous, and high-spirited men. Nor are their abilities, methods, plans, and deliberations inferior to those of Song men; nor is there anyone lacking who might present the proposals of Fu Bi, Fan Zhongyan, Ouyang Xiu, and Su Xun to the reigning sovereign. Recently, the Japanese barbarians have caused trouble, spreading devastation through Wu and Yue. The court has sought out men of wisdom and courage, sparing neither high office nor generous emoluments, in order to quell their…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
亂而卒未聞邊收斬刈芟除之勳以紓
皇上南顧之憂何也愚聞倭夷之入寇也不過
恃其勇悍魚遊鳥宿非有綿翼詭詐不測
之陳也恣其焚燒刼掠滿載而歸非有攻
城爭地之心也所執不過短兵非有中國
之長技也其所以擁護親戚休養生息育
馬牛長子孫愛惜其死非與中國之人異
也然其所至之地相與恐懼流言不戰而
走獸奔鼠竄乞爲囚虜蓋自是中國勇猛
壯健之氣索然無復存矣
===
國家於勳舊之冑養之于太學武弁之子養
之于郡學所以優待功臣不可謂不厚也
文武並設制科而凡閭閻俊乂皆得挾其
射藝以獻之
闕下近日復有廣收豪俠之令其所以取用
之途不可謂不廣也是宜有豪傑之士雲
合而響應矣何久而不聞此忠智之士所
以隱憂而浩嘆也語有之急則寵介冑之
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　三十六
punctuated:
亂，而卒未聞邊收斬刈芟除之勳，以紓皇上南顧之憂，何也？愚聞倭夷之入寇也，不過恃其勇悍，魚遊鳥宿，非有綿翼詭詐不測之陳也；恣其焚燒刼掠，滿載而歸，非有攻城爭地之心也；所執不過短兵，非有中國之長技也。其所以擁護親戚，休養生息，育馬牛，長子孫，愛惜其死，非與中國之人異也。然其所至之地，相與恐懼流言，不戰而走，獸奔鼠竄，乞爲囚虜。蓋自是中國勇猛壯健之氣，索然無復存矣。

國家於勳舊之冑，養之于太學；武弁之子，養之于郡學。所以優待功臣，不可謂不厚也。文武並設制科，而凡閭閻俊乂，皆得挾其射藝以獻之闕下。近日復有廣收豪俠之令，其所以取用之途，不可謂不廣也。是宜有豪傑之士雲合而響應矣，何久而不聞？此忠智之士所以隱憂而浩嘆也。語有之：「急則寵介冑之
translation_en:
…the disorder, yet in the end we have heard of no achievements in cutting down and clearing away the enemy on the frontier [?] to relieve His Majesty’s anxiety as he looks south. Why is this? I have heard that when the Japanese raiders invade, they rely merely on their fierceness and daring. They move like fish and lodge like birds; they have no battle formations of intricately linked wings [?], deception, or unfathomable design. They indulge in burning and plundering, then return fully laden; they have no intention of storming cities and contesting territory. The weapons they wield are merely short weapons; they possess none of China’s superior techniques. In protecting their kin, resting and sustaining their livelihoods, raising horses and cattle, rearing children and grandchildren, and cherishing their lives, they are no different from the people of China. Yet wherever they arrive, people frighten one another and spread rumors, fleeing without a fight, scattering like beasts and scurrying like rats, begging to become captives. Thus China’s spirit of bravery, vigor, and strength has utterly vanished.

The state educates the descendants of its longstanding meritorious servants in the Imperial University, and the sons of military officers in prefectural schools. Its generous treatment of meritorious officials can hardly be called ungenerous. It has established regular examinations in both civil and military subjects, so that all outstanding men from ordinary neighborhoods may bring their skill in archery and present it at the imperial court. Recently, another order has called for the broad recruitment of bold and chivalrous men. The avenues through which men are recruited and employed can hardly be called narrow. Surely, then, heroic men ought to gather like clouds and respond like echoes. Why, after so long, have we heard nothing of them? This is why loyal and discerning men harbor deep anxiety and heave great sighs. As the saying goes: “In times of crisis, favor is bestowed upon men clad in armor…”

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
士寛則寵文學之臣今介胄之士固尊寵
之日矣銜盃躍馬志逸氣浮軒眉攘腕其
初心莫不以攻戰自許也然而身處重屋
出則輿馬暑則張蓋凡所以防患之具莫
不備至求其能犯霜露冒風雪與士卒同
其苦者天下其幾也彼介胄之士何足深
過也天下之爲學士大夫者皆以言兵爲
諱目不辯旌旗耳不習金鼓論戰鬬而股
慄聞戰伐而掩耳涉獵經術炫餙刑名砥
===
厲其小廉曲謹則曰吾以是取卿相足矣
其有能憂國家之急鞠躬盡瘁歷艱險危
亡而不避者天下其幾也天下受禍之地
得一人當之則衆人從而喜曰吾苟免矣
聞有變故則曰此將帥之責非吾事也一
事不請命則劾其專擅府庫之財自一緡
以上稍從便宜以饗將士則有司執案牘
而議其後幸而成事從而分其功不幸而
僨事則文致其罪以逭巳之責其有能推
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　二十七
punctuated: 士，寛則寵文學之臣。」今介胄之士，固尊寵之日矣。銜盃躍馬，志逸氣浮，軒眉攘腕，其初心莫不以攻戰自許也。然而身處重屋，出則輿馬，暑則張蓋，凡所以防患之具，莫不備至。求其能犯霜露、冒風雪，與士卒同其苦者，天下其幾也？彼介胄之士，何足深過也？天下之爲學士大夫者，皆以言兵爲諱，目不辯旌旗，耳不習金鼓，論戰鬬而股慄，聞戰伐而掩耳。涉獵經術，炫餙刑名，砥厲其小廉曲謹，則曰：「吾以是取卿相足矣。」其有能憂國家之急，鞠躬盡瘁，歷艱險危亡而不避者，天下其幾也？天下受禍之地，得一人當之，則衆人從而喜曰：「吾苟免矣。」聞有變故，則曰：「此將帥之責，非吾事也。」一事不請命，則劾其專擅；府庫之財，自一緡以上，稍從便宜以饗將士，則有司執案牘而議其後。幸而成事，從而分其功；不幸而僨事，則文致其罪，以逭巳之責。其有能推
translation_en:
…men in armor; in times of ease, favor is bestowed on ministers of literary learning.” Now is indeed a time when men in armor enjoy honor and favor. Raising their cups and spurring their horses, carefree in ambition and flighty in spirit, lifting their brows and baring their wrists, they all initially profess confidence in their prowess in battle. Yet they dwell in lofty houses, travel by carriage or horse, and have canopies spread over them in the heat. Every provision for shielding them from harm is supplied in full. How many in all the realm can brave frost and dew, face wind and snow, and share the hardships of their soldiers? But why lay excessive blame on these men in armor? Throughout the realm, scholars and officials alike regard discussion of military affairs as taboo. Their eyes cannot distinguish banners and standards; their ears are unaccustomed to gongs and drums. Their thighs tremble at talk of combat, and they cover their ears when they hear of warfare. They dabble in classical learning, make a show of legal and administrative expertise, and cultivate petty integrity and punctilious caution, saying: “With these I have enough to attain the rank of minister or chief councillor.” How many in all the realm can concern themselves with the state's urgent needs, devote themselves utterly to its service, and pass through hardship, danger, and mortal peril without shrinking back?

When a place in the realm suffers calamity and one person is found to bear the burden, everyone else rejoices, saying: “At least I have escaped.” When they hear of an emergency, they say: “This is the responsibility of the commanders; it is no affair of mine.” If a commander acts in even one matter without requesting authorization, they impeach him for arrogating power. If he exercises the slightest discretion in using treasury funds, even a single string of cash or more, to reward his officers and soldiers, the responsible officials seize upon the documents and criticize him afterward. If he fortunately succeeds, they come forward to share his credit; if he unfortunately fails, they contrive charges against him to evade their own responsibility. As for those able to extend…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
同舟之誼殫心戮力期於必濟成不以爲
功敗則共受其罰者天下其幾也此忠智
之士其心於小就不樂以軍功自顯也漢
人有言曰天下安注意相天下危注意將
將相調和則士豫附此猶分將相爲二也
古者六軍之制軍將皆命卿無事則將歸
卿列有事則諸卿皆將入則典司政本出
則經營四方此召虎之所以平淮南而皇
父程伯休父之所以省徐土也今之總督
===
大臣卽其任也然而今日之所謂清班異
軸所儲育以爲輔養啓沃之助者蓋皆具
文武之材足以戡禍定亂者也凡錢穀刑
名瑣屑之務夫旣不以勞之矣而亦未聞
有出而經營四方者何也今夫拔劍而起
挺身而鬬謂文學之士不能是誠不能也
察幾審勢校計索情則聰明磊落之士所
可彊勉宜不出介胄之下也天下之所最
難且重者莫若將帥之任必須大破常格
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄 二十八
punctuated: 同舟之誼，殫心戮力，期於必濟，成不以爲功，敗則共受其罰者，天下其幾也？此忠智之士，其心於小就，不樂以軍功自顯也。漢人有言曰：「天下安，注意相；天下危，注意將。將相調和，則士豫附。」此猶分將相爲二也。古者六軍之制，軍將皆命卿，無事則將歸卿列，有事則諸卿皆將。入則典司政本，出則經營四方。此召虎之所以平淮南，而皇父、程伯休父之所以省徐土也。今之總督大臣，卽其任也。然而今日之所謂清班異軸，所儲育以爲輔養啓沃之助者，蓋皆具文武之材，足以戡禍定亂者也。凡錢穀刑名瑣屑之務，夫旣不以勞之矣，而亦未聞有出而經營四方者，何也？今夫拔劍而起，挺身而鬬，謂文學之士不能，是誠不能也。察幾審勢，校計索情，則聰明磊落之士所可彊勉，宜不出介胄之下也。天下之所最難且重者，莫若將帥之任，必須大破常格。
translation_en:
…the solidarity of those sharing a boat, devote their hearts and unite their strength in the determination to bring the undertaking to success, claim no credit when it succeeds, and share the punishment when it fails—how many such people are there in the realm? Thus loyal and wise men set their hearts on modest accomplishments [?] and take no pleasure in distinguishing themselves through military merit. A man of the Han said: “When the realm is at peace, attention rests on the chief minister; when the realm is in danger, attention rests on the general. When general and chief minister work in harmony, the officers readily give their allegiance.” Yet this still treats generals and chief ministers as two separate groups.

Under the ancient system of six armies, the army commanders were all appointed ministers. When there was no trouble, the commanders returned to the ranks of the ministers; when trouble arose, the ministers all served as commanders. At court they directed the fundamentals of government; outside it they conducted affairs throughout the four quarters. This was how Shao Hu pacified Huainan, and how Huangfu and Chengbo Xiufu inspected the lands of Xu. The high officials serving today as supreme commanders hold precisely this responsibility.

Yet those who today occupy what are called prestigious ranks and exceptional positions [?], cultivated and held in reserve to assist in nurturing and enlightening the sovereign, surely all possess both civil and military abilities sufficient to quell calamity and restore order. They are already spared the burden of such petty duties as revenue administration and judicial business. Why, then, do we never hear of any going out to conduct affairs throughout the four quarters? If one says that men of literary learning cannot draw their swords, spring up, and thrust themselves into battle, then indeed they cannot. But discerning the first signs of change, assessing circumstances, comparing plans, and probing the true situation are things that intelligent, high-minded men can strive to accomplish. In these they should be no less capable than men in armor and helmets. No responsibility in the realm is more difficult or weighty than that of military command; we must therefore break decisively with the usual rules…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
自公侯之貴以及行伍之賤自臺閣之近
以及郡國之遠自卿輔之尊以及罪廢隱
淪之卑不問其類凡有將能者用而試之
一如陸贄所云敦以付授之義固以親信
之恩假以便宜之權待以殊常之賞其卑
賤且遠者皆取其大節而略其細過待以
不次之位則人莫不感激思奮講求戰伐
之具智者騁謀勇者効力而真材可得也
第二問
===
黃文獻
馬上中六箭
步下中三箭
兵無常形也而制勝之道存乎法法無常
用也而通變之妙存乎機夫兵有虛實之
異而法也者所以爲制勝萬全之策法有
常變之異而機也者所以妙通變不窮之
術是故有分有合有正有奇者法也法之
所在利則動不利則止因形以制勝而吾
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　三十九
punctuated:
自公侯之貴以及行伍之賤，自臺閣之近以及郡國之遠，自卿輔之尊以及罪廢隱淪之卑，不問其類，凡有將能者，用而試之。一如陸贄所云，敦以付授之義，固以親信之恩，假以便宜之權，待以殊常之賞。其卑賤且遠者，皆取其大節而略其細過，待以不次之位，則人莫不感激思奮，講求戰伐之具，智者騁謀，勇者効力，而真材可得也。
第二問
黃文獻：馬上中六箭，步下中三箭。
兵無常形也，而制勝之道存乎法；法無常用也，而通變之妙存乎機。夫兵有虛實之異，而法也者，所以爲制勝萬全之策；法有常變之異，而機也者，所以妙通變不窮之術。是故有分有合、有正有奇者，法也。法之所在，利則動，不利則止，因形以制勝，而吾
translation_en:
…from the nobility of dukes and marquises to the lowly ranks of ordinary soldiers; from those close at hand in the central government to those far away in the prefectures and regions; from the exalted ranks of ministers and chief councillors to the humble condition of those dismissed for offenses or living in obscurity. Regardless of their category, all who possess the abilities of a commander should be employed and put to the test. Follow precisely what Lu Zhi said: strengthen their commitment through the moral obligation of an entrusted charge; secure their loyalty through the favor of personal trust; grant them authority to act as circumstances require; and accord them exceptional rewards. For those of humble status and those far away, value their integrity in major matters and overlook their minor faults, granting them positions outside the normal sequence of promotion. Then everyone will be moved by gratitude and eager to exert themselves, studying the means of warfare. The intelligent will deploy their strategies, the brave will devote their strength, and true talent can be obtained.

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
之用兵也敵不可勝以正爲奇以奇爲正
分而能合合而能分者機也機之所在或
用法或不用法相宜以制權而吾之决勝
也人不能測夫兵可以易言哉其强也或
示之以弱其虛也或示之以實呼吸之頃
變化難測苟徒執一定之形以爲得敵之
情守一定之法而昧變通之術如之何而
不僨軍敗事也古之善戰者知兵之形無
常而法之用不可泥也故其用兵也不違
===
乎法而亦不拘於法不違乎法是謂有制
之兵不拘乎法是謂知變之兵兵而至於
知變焉則不待戰而勝負之勢以分不待
陣而成敗之迹以决法曰人知我所以勝
之形而莫知吾所以致勝之形又曰因敵
變化而取勝者謂之神嗚呼非知用兵之
機者其孰能與於斯請因明問而陳之宋
子罕曰兵者所以威不軌而昭文德也天
生五材民並用之誰能去兵是國不可以
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　三十
punctuated:
之用兵也，敵不可勝。以正爲奇，以奇爲正，分而能合，合而能分者，機也。機之所在，或用法，或不用法，相宜以制權，而吾之决勝也，人不能測。夫兵可以易言哉？其强也，或示之以弱；其虛也，或示之以實。呼吸之頃，變化難測。苟徒執一定之形，以爲得敵之情，守一定之法，而昧變通之術，如之何而不僨軍敗事也？古之善戰者，知兵之形無常，而法之用不可泥也。故其用兵也，不違乎法，而亦不拘於法。不違乎法，是謂有制之兵；不拘乎法，是謂知變之兵。兵而至於知變焉，則不待戰而勝負之勢以分，不待陣而成敗之迹以决。法曰：「人知我所以勝之形，而莫知吾所以致勝之形。」又曰：「因敵變化而取勝者，謂之神。」嗚呼！非知用兵之機者，其孰能與於斯？請因明問而陳之。
宋子罕曰：「兵者，所以威不軌而昭文德也。天生五材，民並用之，誰能去兵？」是國不可以
translation_en:
…in my employment of troops, the enemy cannot overcome me. To turn the orthodox into the unorthodox and the unorthodox into the orthodox, to be able to unite after dividing and divide after uniting—this is mastery of opportunity. As opportunity dictates, one sometimes employs established methods and sometimes sets them aside, weighing expedients according to what suits the circumstances; thus others cannot fathom how I secure victory. Can warfare be spoken of lightly? When strong, one may display weakness; when one's forces are insubstantial, one may display strength. Within a single breath, changes become impossible to fathom. If one merely clings to a fixed disposition, believing that one has grasped the enemy's circumstances, and adheres to a fixed method while remaining ignorant of the art of adaptation, how can one avoid bringing the army to ruin and the undertaking to failure? Those of old who excelled in warfare knew that military dispositions have no constant form and that methods must not be applied rigidly. Thus, in employing troops, they neither departed from established methods nor were constrained by them. Not departing from established methods is what is called having an army governed by order; not being constrained by them is what is called having an army that understands adaptation. Once an army understands adaptation, the balance of victory and defeat is already determined before battle, and the course of success and failure is already settled before the formations are drawn up. The Art of War says: “Others know the disposition by which I win, but none knows the disposition by which I bring victory about.” It also says: “One who wins victory by adapting to the enemy is called divine.” Ah! Who could attain this without understanding how to seize opportunities in employing troops? Permit me to elaborate in response to your illuminating question.
Zihan of Song said: “Arms are the means by which to overawe the lawless and make manifest civil virtue. Heaven produces the five materials, and the people use them all: who can dispense with arms?” Thus, a state cannot…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
無兵也尚矣然兩壘相望而强弱分焉兩
陣相角而勝敗分焉安危治亂之判係於
善用與不善用之間耳則爲將者之不可
以不知兵也亦尚矣三代之兵以義而動
以正而行未聞有虛實奇正之法春秋戰
國之時列國互相征伐于是談兵之士各
騁其權謀詐力之說以爲强國威民之術
而兵法始興於古矣至於後之折衝禦侮
之士皆不能外之以制勝成功焉然法一
===
也有用之而勝者亦有不用而勝者若是
者豈法不足以盡兵之用乎蓋用兵者法
也用法者機也機之爲用所以妙變化于
不測通應務于不窮而運用乎法者也使
法而無機則法有時而窮矣是故敵勢强
而可以計分之敵氣挫而可以兵迫之此
戰之機也知機之可戰則循法而戰可也
或法不宜戰而戰亦可也敵無求戰之意
而可以間致之敵不虞吾之來而可以急
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄 三十
punctuated: 無兵也尚矣。然兩壘相望而强弱分焉，兩陣相角而勝敗分焉，安危治亂之判，係於善用與不善用之間耳。則爲將者之不可以不知兵也，亦尚矣。三代之兵，以義而動，以正而行，未聞有虛實奇正之法。春秋戰國之時，列國互相征伐，于是談兵之士，各騁其權謀詐力之說，以爲强國威民之術，而兵法始興於古矣。至於後之折衝禦侮之士，皆不能外之以制勝成功焉。然法一也，有用之而勝者，亦有不用而勝者。若是者，豈法不足以盡兵之用乎？蓋用兵者，法也；用法者，機也。機之爲用，所以妙變化于不測，通應務于不窮，而運用乎法者也。使法而無機，則法有時而窮矣。是故敵勢强而可以計分之，敵氣挫而可以兵迫之，此戰之機也。知機之可戰，則循法而戰可也，或法不宜戰而戰亦可也。敵無求戰之意而可以間致之，敵不虞吾之來而可以急
translation_en: …do without armed forces: this has long been recognized. Yet when two fortified camps face one another, their relative strength becomes apparent; when two battle formations clash, victory and defeat are determined. The distinction between security and peril, order and disorder, depends solely on whether armed forces are employed well or poorly. Thus it has likewise long been recognized that a commander cannot afford to lack knowledge of warfare. The armies of the Three Dynasties mobilized in accordance with righteousness and proceeded in accordance with rectitude; one does not hear of methods involving emptiness and solidity, or unconventional and conventional operations. During the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, the various states attacked one another. Those who discoursed on warfare then each promoted their doctrines of stratagem, deception, and force as techniques for strengthening states and overawing the people. Thus military methods first flourished in antiquity. Later, those who repelled attacks and resisted aggression could not dispense with these methods in securing victory and achieving success. Yet although the methods are the same, some win by employing them, while others win without employing them. If this is so, could it be that methods cannot encompass every application of military force? Methods govern the employment of troops; timely judgment governs the employment of methods. Such judgment enables one to respond with subtlety to unpredictable changes, deal inexhaustibly with unfolding affairs, and put methods into practice. If there are methods but no timely judgment, those methods will sometimes reach their limits. Thus, when the enemy’s position is strong but a stratagem can divide his forces, or when his morale is broken and troops can press him hard, these are opportunities for battle. Recognizing an opportunity to fight, one may follow established methods and fight; one may also fight even when those methods counsel against it. When the enemy has no intention of seeking battle but can be induced to do so through covert means, or when the enemy does not anticipate our arrival and swift action can…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
乘之此攻之機也知機之可攻則循法而
攻可也或法不宜攻而攻亦可也敵利於
急而可以緩牽之敵知吾怯而可以銳襲
之此守之機也知機之可守則循法而守
可也或法不宜守而守亦可也吾惟執其
機以應變而至於法之合不合何足以泥
之哉故縱横疾徐不失其馳御之法也而
王良之御則上下出入不拘拘于馳驅之
範而所獲滋多矣寒暑虛實不違其證醫
===
之法也而盧扁之醫則胗療攻治不拘拘
于劑砭之方而得効奇中矣於藝且然而
况於兵乎攷之於古若步兵依丘陵易地
則用騎法也李嗣源潛行山中大破契丹
而遂解幽州之圍周德威退軍平原大敗
梁軍而遂成鄗邑之績非與自戰其地爲
散爲客務入則專法也慕容德納韓諄之
言嬰城固守而後魏卒不能加兵陳餘棄
左車之畫空壁出戰而韓信遂以之滅趙
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　三十二
punctuated:
乘之，此攻之機也。知機之可攻，則循法而攻可也，或法不宜攻而攻亦可也。敵利於急，而可以緩牽之；敵知吾怯，而可以銳襲之，此守之機也。知機之可守，則循法而守可也，或法不宜守而守亦可也。吾惟執其機以應變，而至於法之合不合，何足以泥之哉？故縱横疾徐，不失其馳御之法也，而王良之御，則上下出入，不拘拘于馳驅之範，而所獲滋多矣。寒暑虛實，不違其證醫之法也，而盧扁之醫，則胗療攻治，不拘拘于劑砭之方，而得効奇中矣。於藝且然，而况於兵乎？

攷之於古，若步兵依丘陵，易地則用騎，法也。李嗣源潛行山中，大破契丹，而遂解幽州之圍；周德威退軍平原，大敗梁軍，而遂成鄗邑之績，非與？自戰其地爲散，爲客務入則專，法也。慕容德納韓諄之言，嬰城固守，而後魏卒不能加兵；陳餘棄左車之畫，空壁出戰，而韓信遂以之滅趙
translation_en:
…take advantage of them with a sudden attack: this is an opportunity for offensive action. When one recognizes an opportunity to attack, one may attack in accordance with established rules; one may also attack when the rules counsel against it. When the enemy benefits from swift action, one can hold him back through delay; when the enemy believes us timid, one can strike him with vigor. These are opportunities in defense. When one recognizes an opportunity to defend, one may defend in accordance with the rules; one may also defend when the rules counsel against it. I would simply seize the opportunity to respond to changing circumstances. Whether this accords with the rules or not—how could that warrant being bound by them? Thus, whether moving across or along, swiftly or slowly, one keeps to the rules of chariot driving. Yet Wang Liang, in his driving, went up and down, in and out, without rigidly adhering to the prescribed patterns, and his haul of game grew all the greater. In treating cold and heat, depletion and repletion, one does not depart from the rules of diagnosis and treatment. Yet physicians such as Lu and Bian [?], in examining, treating, and combating illness, did not rigidly adhere to prescriptions for medicines and stone needles, and achieved remarkably apt results. If this is so even in these arts, how much more so in warfare!

Consider examples from antiquity. That infantry should rely on hills and that cavalry should be used on level ground is an established rule. Yet did not Li Siyuan advance secretly through the mountains, inflict a crushing defeat on the Qidan, and thereby relieve the siege of Youzhou? And did not Zhou Dewei withdraw his army onto the plain, inflict a crushing defeat on the Liang army, and thereby achieve his victory at Haoyi? That troops fighting in their own territory are on dispersive ground, while an invading army becomes united by penetrating deeply, is an established rule. Murong De accepted Han Zhun’s advice and held fast within the city walls, so that the Later Wei ultimately could not attack him. Chen Yu rejected Zuoche’s plan, emptied his fortifications, and marched out to fight, whereupon Han Xin took advantage of this to destroy Zhao…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
非與形人而我無形致人而不致於人法
也耿弇以間誘費邑之救遂平四十餘營
而定齊南曹操以疑分袁紹之兵遂解白
馬之圍而斬驍將非與若是者固法之所
可勝而亦機之所必勝焉何也契丹圍久
而師老景仁遠出而軍疲固有可勝之機
也而嗣源德威以有制之兵應之其制勝
必矣大武遠涉以貪利陳餘自矜而輕敵
固有取敗之機也而慕容德韓信以得筭
===
之兵制之其取勝宜矣費邑從逆而抗王
師袁紹忌能而廢群策固法之所忌而機
可敗也而耿弇曹操以先勝之兵攻之又
豈有不勝者乎故以法而戰則克者嗣源
德威曹操是也以法而攻則取者韓信耿
弇是也以法而守則固者慕容德是也此
之謂取必于法者也以不用法而勝者言
之兵不貴久師出以律法也然高宗奮伐
荆楚遲以三年而後成功霍去病六出匈
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　三十二
punctuated:
非與？形人而我無形，致人而不致於人，法也。耿弇以間誘費邑之救，遂平四十餘營而定齊南；曹操以疑分袁紹之兵，遂解白馬之圍而斬驍將，非與？若是者，固法之所可勝，而亦機之所必勝焉。何也？契丹圍久而師老，景仁遠出而軍疲，固有可勝之機也，而嗣源、德威以有制之兵應之，其制勝必矣。大武遠涉以貪利，陳餘自矜而輕敵，固有取敗之機也，而慕容德、韓信以得筭之兵制之，其取勝宜矣。費邑從逆而抗王師，袁紹忌能而廢群策，固法之所忌而機可敗也，而耿弇、曹操以先勝之兵攻之，又豈有不勝者乎？故以法而戰則克者，嗣源、德威、曹操是也；以法而攻則取者，韓信、耿弇是也；以法而守則固者，慕容德是也。此之謂取必于法者也。
以不用法而勝者言之，兵不貴久，師出以律，法也。然高宗奮伐荆楚，遲以三年而後成功；霍去病六出匈
translation_en:
…was this not so? To make the enemy reveal his dispositions while keeping one’s own concealed, and to compel the enemy’s movements without being compelled by him: these are principles of warfare. Geng Yan used a ruse to lure Fei Yi into coming to the rescue, then subdued more than forty camps and pacified Qinan [?]. Cao Cao used a diversion to divide Yuan Shao’s forces, then relieved the siege of Baima and slew his valiant general. Was this not so? In such cases, established principles made victory possible, while the circumstances made victory certain. Why? The Khitan forces had maintained their siege so long that their troops were worn out; Jingren had marched far afield, leaving his army exhausted. These circumstances offered opportunities to defeat them. Siyuan and Dewei met them with disciplined troops, and their victory was assured. Dawu [?; probably Taiwu] had journeyed far in pursuit of gain, while Chen Yu was conceited and underestimated his enemy. These circumstances contained the seeds of defeat. Murong De and Han Xin overcame them with armies whose calculations secured the advantage, so their victories were to be expected. Fei Yi followed rebels and resisted the royal army; Yuan Shao resented able men and rejected the counsels of his advisers. These were precisely the errors that military principles warn against, and the circumstances made them vulnerable to defeat. Geng Yan and Cao Cao attacked them with armies that had secured the conditions for victory beforehand. How could they have failed to win? Thus, those who fought according to established principles and prevailed were Siyuan, Dewei, and Cao Cao; those who attacked according to these principles and captured their objectives were Han Xin and Geng Yan; and the one who defended according to these principles and held firm was Murong De. This is what is meant by securing certainty through established principles.
As for those who won without following established principles: that warfare should not be prolonged, and that an army should go forth under discipline, are principles of warfare. Yet Gaozong launched a vigorous campaign against Jing-Chu and achieved success only after three long years; Huo Qubing made six expeditions against the Xiong…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
奴不用古法而皆奏捷則與法異矣戰隆
勿登禁祥去疑法也然陸遜覆先主於馬
鞍山遂破益兵而保夷陵田单以一卒爲
神師遂破燕軍而復宗國則與法殊矣甬
水必俟定而涉風逆必堅陣以待法也然
李靖之下江陵乘江水之漲而遂成功符
彥卿之戰契丹因風勢之逆而遂逐北則
與法不同矣若是者皆法之所忌而卒能
取勝者蓋法雖不合而機則可勝耳何也
===
荆楚之負固不庭既有可伐之罪而高宗
以中興之師臨之又有必克之理則雖持
久而卒能底績匈奴剽悍輕鬬本不可以
法制之而去病方略素定固豫有常勝之
筭則雖無古法而亦能致勝先主連營七
百里既犯可敗之形而陸遜連破四十營
已成破竹之勢此所以犯險而亦勝也樂
毅以�七奔趙燕人既有土崩之勢而田单
激怒其民齊人且切復讐之憤此所以用
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　三四
punctuated:
奴，不用古法而皆奏捷，則與法異矣。戰隆勿登，禁祥去疑，法也。然陸遜覆先主於馬鞍山，遂破益兵而保夷陵；田单以一卒爲神師，遂破燕軍而復宗國，則與法殊矣。甬水必俟定而涉，風逆必堅陣以待，法也。然李靖之下江陵，乘江水之漲而遂成功；符彥卿之戰契丹，因風勢之逆而遂逐北，則與法不同矣。若是者，皆法之所忌而卒能取勝者，蓋法雖不合，而機則可勝耳。何也？

荆楚之負固不庭，既有可伐之罪，而高宗以中興之師臨之，又有必克之理，則雖持久而卒能底績。匈奴剽悍輕鬬，本不可以法制之，而去病方略素定，固豫有常勝之筭，則雖無古法而亦能致勝。先主連營七百里，既犯可敗之形，而陸遜連破四十營，已成破竹之勢，此所以犯險而亦勝也。樂毅以�七奔趙，燕人既有土崩之勢，而田单激怒其民，齊人且切復讐之憤，此所以用

The Xiongnu were fierce and swift, readily entering battle, and could not in the first place be subdued through prescribed rules.
