title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
詭而有成也蕭銑竊據一隅不足以當中
國之師而李靖因江水之漲知其必不設
備則水固有以助其成功也契丹深入寇
掠既犯貪利之戒而符彥卿因風勢之逆
知其可以計襲則風固有以助其致勝也
故攻不以法而取者有若高宗李靖田單
也戰不以法而克者有若去病陸遜也守
不以法而固者有若符彥卿也是皆不合
乎法而取必于機者也是知勝敵者不在
===
於力而在於法用法者不拘於法而在於
機機之與法蓋互相爲用矣然有得於機
未有無得於法者也何也彼用法者固無
容議矣而不用法者要其極而論之亦未
嘗不與法合焉是故荆楚之伐非所謂其
徐如林者乎六出之捷非所謂能而示之
不能者乎馬鞍之麾非所謂因勢破之者
乎卽墨之戰非所謂愚士卒之耳目使之
無知者乎江陵之下非所謂攻其無備者
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　三十五
punctuated:
詭而有成也。蕭銑竊據一隅，不足以當中國之師，而李靖因江水之漲，知其必不設備，則水固有以助其成功也。契丹深入寇掠，既犯貪利之戒，而符彥卿因風勢之逆，知其可以計襲，則風固有以助其致勝也。故攻不以法而取者，有若高宗、李靖、田單也；戰不以法而克者，有若去病、陸遜也；守不以法而固者，有若符彥卿也。是皆不合乎法而取必于機者也。是知勝敵者不在於力而在於法，用法者不拘於法而在於機，機之與法蓋互相爲用矣。
然有得於機，未有無得於法者也。何也？彼用法者固無容議矣，而不用法者，要其極而論之，亦未嘗不與法合焉。是故荆楚之伐，非所謂「其徐如林」者乎？六出之捷，非所謂「能而示之不能」者乎？馬鞍之麾，非所謂「因勢破之」者乎？卽墨之戰，非所謂「愚士卒之耳目，使之無知」者乎？江陵之下，非所謂「攻其無備」者
translation_en:
…deception could thus bring success. Xiao Xian had usurped control of a single corner of the realm and was no match for the armies of the Central Lands. Li Jing, observing the river’s rise, knew that Xiao would certainly make no defensive preparations; thus the water indeed helped him achieve success. The Khitan penetrated deep into the country to plunder, thereby violating the injunction against greed for gain. Fu Yanqing, observing that the wind was against him, knew he could launch a surprise attack through stratagem; thus the wind indeed helped him achieve victory. Those who captured their objectives while attacking without following established methods include Gaozong, Li Jing, and Tian Dan; those who won battles without following established methods include Qubing and Lu Xun; and those who secured their defenses without following established methods include Fu Yanqing. All these departed from established methods but secured success by grasping the opportune moment. From this we know that defeating an enemy depends on methods rather than strength, and that applying methods depends on grasping the opportune moment rather than adhering rigidly to them. Opportunity and method thus serve one another.
Yet no one who has grasped the opportune moment has failed also to grasp established methods. Why is this? Those who follow established methods of course require no discussion. As for those who do not, if we consider their actions in light of their ultimate outcome, they too have never failed to accord with those methods. Thus, was not the campaign against Jingchu an instance of the saying, “When moving slowly, be like a forest”? Were not the victories in six expeditions an instance of “When capable, show yourself incapable”? Was not the direction of troops at Ma’an an instance of “Exploit the situation to defeat them”? Was not the battle of Jimo an instance of “Befuddle the eyes and ears of the officers and soldiers, keeping them ignorant”? Was not the capture of Jiangling an instance of “Attack where they are unprepared”…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
乎陽城之勝非所謂出其不意者乎此之
謂有得於機必有得於法也然所謂機者
又豈外於料敵以設奇乎法曰知己知彼
百戰不殆料敵之說也又曰因敵轉化不
爲事先設奇之說也策之而知得失之計
作之而知動靜之理形之而知死生之地
角之而知有餘不足之處此明於料敵者
也則未戰而得筭多法何足以拘之矣利
而誘之亂而取之佚能勞之安能動之此
===
妙於設奇者也則因形以措勝于衆衆不
能知法何足以泥之矣是故不能料敵則
不能設奇而勝負之筭悖不能設奇則不
可謂之料敵而變化之妙窒故用兵非難
料敵爲難用法非難設奇爲難能料敵則
能審機矣能設奇則能握機矣
執事所謂權勿預定變勿先圖與時遷移
應物變化非隨機應變之謂耶雖然用兵
之道在法而用法之權在將將得其人則
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄 三十六
punctuated:
乎？陽城之勝，非所謂出其不意者乎？此之謂有得於機，必有得於法也。然所謂機者，又豈外於料敵以設奇乎？法曰：「知己知彼，百戰不殆。」料敵之說也。又曰：「因敵轉化，不爲事先。」設奇之說也。策之而知得失之計，作之而知動靜之理，形之而知死生之地，角之而知有餘不足之處，此明於料敵者也。則未戰而得筭多，法何足以拘之矣？利而誘之，亂而取之，佚能勞之，安能動之，此妙於設奇者也。則因形以措勝于衆，衆不能知，法何足以泥之矣？是故不能料敵，則不能設奇，而勝負之筭悖；不能設奇，則不可謂之料敵，而變化之妙窒。故用兵非難，料敵爲難；用法非難，設奇爲難。能料敵，則能審機矣；能設奇，則能握機矣。
執事所謂「權勿預定，變勿先圖，與時遷移，應物變化」，非隨機應變之謂耶？雖然，用兵之道在法，而用法之權在將。將得其人，則
translation_en:
…was it not? Was the victory at Yangcheng not an instance of what is called “striking where the enemy does not expect it”? This is what it means to say that whoever grasps the opportune moment must also grasp military principles. Yet how could this opportune moment lie outside assessing the enemy and devising unorthodox tactics? The military principles say: “Know yourself and know your enemy, and in a hundred battles you will not be imperiled.” This concerns assessing the enemy. They also say: “Adapt and transform in accordance with the enemy; do not act ahead of events.” This concerns devising unorthodox tactics. Probe the enemy to discover the calculations governing gain and loss; stir him to discover the principles governing movement and stillness; make him reveal his dispositions to discover the ground of life and death; test him to discover where he has a surplus and where he is deficient. These are instances of clear understanding in assessing the enemy. Thus, even before battle, one has many calculations in favor of victory: how could military principles suffice to constrain such a person? Entice the enemy with profit; seize him when he is in disorder; when he is rested, make him toil; when he is secure, make him move. These are instances of mastery in devising unorthodox tactics. Thus one secures victory according to the dispositions before the multitude, yet the multitude cannot understand it. How could military principles suffice to fetter such a person? Therefore, if one cannot assess the enemy, one cannot devise unorthodox tactics, and calculations of victory and defeat go awry. If one cannot devise unorthodox tactics, one cannot be said to assess the enemy, and mastery of adaptation is obstructed. Thus employing troops is not difficult; assessing the enemy is difficult. Applying military principles is not difficult; devising unorthodox tactics is difficult. If one can assess the enemy, one can discern the opportune moment. If one can devise unorthodox tactics, one can seize that moment.
What you, honored examiners, call “Do not determine expedient measures beforehand or plan changes in advance; shift with the times and transform in response to circumstances”—does this not mean responding to changes as opportunities arise? Even so, the way of employing troops lies in military principles, while authority to apply those principles rests with the commander. If the right person is chosen as commander, then…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
國輔既周制勝有術卽法之合不合無論
也故將者上知天道下知地理中知人事
本之以忠義行之以智勇如法所謂五事
五才闕一不可也是故不知三軍之事而
同三軍之政則軍士惑矣不知三軍之權
而同三軍之任則軍士疑矣是謂之亂軍
引勝也傳曰君不擇將以其國予敵也然
則擇將者非用兵之先務耶
論
===
善用兵者脩道而保法
李楫
馬上中五箭
步下中二箭
用兵之要無他惟於不可勝者圖之而已何也
自夫聯屬人情者之謂道整齊衆志者之謂法
脩道以示恩也而使之知愛保法以示威也而
使之知畏知愛則不忍離知畏則不敢玩並施
而不悖相濟以有成則在我常有餘在敵常不
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　三十七
punctuated:
國輔既周，制勝有術，卽法之合不合，無論也。故將者，上知天道，下知地理，中知人事，本之以忠義，行之以智勇，如法所謂五事五才，闕一不可也。是故不知三軍之事而同三軍之政，則軍士惑矣；不知三軍之權而同三軍之任，則軍士疑矣。是謂之亂軍引勝也。傳曰：「君不擇將，以其國予敵也。」然則擇將者，非用兵之先務耶？
論
善用兵者脩道而保法
李楫
馬上中五箭，步下中二箭。
用兵之要無他，惟於不可勝者圖之而已。何也？自夫聯屬人情者之謂道，整齊衆志者之謂法。脩道以示恩也，而使之知愛；保法以示威也，而使之知畏。知愛則不忍離，知畏則不敢玩。並施而不悖，相濟以有成，則在我常有餘，在敵常不
translation_en:
…the support of the state is comprehensive, and there are means of securing victory; whether these accord with established methods need not even be discussed. Thus a general must understand the Way of Heaven above, the patterns of the earth below, and human affairs between them. He must ground his conduct in loyalty and righteousness and act with wisdom and courage. Of what military doctrine calls the five considerations and the five talents, not one may be lacking. Thus, if one shares in administering the armies without understanding their affairs, the soldiers become bewildered; if one shares responsibility for the armies without understanding their discretionary use of power, the soldiers become doubtful. This is called throwing the army into disorder and bringing victory to the enemy. A transmitted text says: “A ruler who fails to choose his generals hands his state over to the enemy.” Is choosing generals, then, not the foremost task in employing troops?
Discourse
“One Skilled in Employing Troops Cultivates the Way and Upholds Regulations”
Li Ji 李楫
He scored five hits with arrows on horseback and two on foot.
The essential point in employing troops is simply to plan how to make oneself invincible. Why is this? What binds human sentiments together is called the Way; what brings the wills of the multitude into order is called regulations. Cultivating the Way displays benevolence and teaches them affection; upholding regulations displays authority and teaches them fear. Knowing affection, they cannot bear to leave; knowing fear, they dare not be negligent. When both are applied without conflict and complement each other to achieve success, our side will always have a surplus of strength, while the enemy will always lack…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
足輕重之分已定而利鈍之勢自殊戰守攻圍
舉而措之裕如也所謂先爲不可勝以待敵之
可勝明乎此者其知用兵之要者歟夫兵何始
乎人生有欲欲熾則爭爭而不已乃鬬智角力
相率而趨於詭道縱横闔闢之習滋詛欺陵軋
之風靡矣兵之盛世之衰也故吾用吾之民不
免驅之死地而加之於敵亦欲握其命而坐制
之也固仁人之所甚隱人心豈樂於從事哉易
曰豫順以動又曰毒天下而民從之是必伏至
===
險於大順而寂妄動於至和斯民之從之也如
頤指之便隨其所使而不拂也君子之處此當
必有要焉矣孫子之言曰道者令民與上同意
可與死生而不畏危法者曲制官道主用也是
故善用兵者貴脩而保之者也夫道自我出何
事於脩法自我議何事於保蓋上下之情苦於
睽懸而輕忽慓悍士之氣每易盈而難制也使
有所及有所不及其情必孤故脩之如比跡葺
間人人而聯屬之也有所守有所不守其法必
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　三十八
punctuated:
足，輕重之分已定，而利鈍之勢自殊，戰守攻圍，舉而措之裕如也。所謂「先爲不可勝，以待敵之可勝」，明乎此者，其知用兵之要者歟！夫兵何始乎？人生有欲，欲熾則爭，爭而不已，乃鬬智角力，相率而趨於詭道，縱横闔闢之習滋詛，欺陵軋之風靡矣。兵之盛，世之衰也。故吾用吾之民，不免驅之死地，而加之於敵，亦欲握其命而坐制之也。固仁人之所甚隱，人心豈樂於從事哉！易曰：「豫，順以動。」又曰：「毒天下而民從之。」是必伏至險於大順，而寂妄動於至和，斯民之從之也，如頤指之便，隨其所使而不拂也。君子之處此，當必有要焉矣。

孫子之言曰：「道者，令民與上同意，可與死生而不畏危；法者，曲制、官道、主用也。」是故善用兵者，貴脩而保之者也。夫道自我出，何事於脩？法自我議，何事於保？蓋上下之情苦於睽懸，而輕忽慓悍，士之氣每易盈而難制也。使有所及，有所不及，其情必孤，故脩之如比跡葺間，人人而聯屬之也。有所守，有所不守，其法必
translation_en:
…insufficient. Once the relative balance of strength has been settled, the prospects of success and failure naturally differ; whether in battle, defense, assault, or siege, one can act with ample ease. This is what is meant by “first making oneself invincible, and then awaiting the enemy’s vulnerability.” Does not someone who understands this know the essentials of employing troops? How did warfare begin? Human beings have desires; when desires grow intense, contention follows. When contention does not cease, people pit their wits and strength against one another, leading each other onto the path of deception. Practices of maneuvering through alliances and shifting combinations proliferate [?], while bullying and oppression become prevalent. The flourishing of warfare marks the decline of the age. Thus, when I employ my people, I cannot avoid driving them into mortal danger; and when I bring them against the enemy, I likewise seek to hold the enemy’s life in my hands and control him at ease. This is surely a source of profound distress to the benevolent. How could the human heart take pleasure in such an undertaking? The Book of Changes says: “Yu: moving in accordance with what is right.” It also says: “He brings suffering upon all under Heaven, yet the people follow him.” One must therefore subdue the utmost danger through complete accord, and still reckless action through perfect harmony. Then the people follow as readily as if directed by a movement of the chin, going wherever they are sent without resistance. A gentleman dealing with this must surely have an essential principle.

Sunzi says: “The Way causes the people to share the intentions of their superiors, so that they can join them in death and life without fearing danger. Regulations concern military organization, the duties of officers, and the management of supplies.” Thus, those skilled in employing troops prize cultivating the Way and maintaining regulations. But if the Way issues from me, what need is there to cultivate it? If regulations are deliberated by me, what need is there to maintain them? The difficulty is that the feelings of superiors and subordinates become estranged and widely separated; moreover, soldiers are heedless and fierce, and their spirit readily swells beyond restraint. If care reaches some but fails to reach others, their affections will become isolated. Thus one cultivates the Way as though aligning footsteps and repairing gaps [?], binding them together person by person. If some regulations are observed and others are not, those regulations will inevitably…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
廢故保之如捧盈持重人人而整齊之也道以
通其幽恩之所以維也法以振其顯威之所以
御也平時鼓舞而綱紀之固將託以生死而恃
爲存亡矣今夫同舟而濟者百族之子呼同聲
招同臂率遇風波迅以破之而歡然利涉其情
同也群舉以獵獸可丘陵而必範我馳驅寧少
而不務多者法不可弛也況用兵乎今之談兵
者孰不曰察九地之利害辯五行之生尅明奇
正之變化覘主客之堅瑕勵士以作其氣用間
===
以抒其謀棄實以擊其虛因形以布其勢如是
可以爲兵矣而不知以逸待勞以靜馭動之要
則不在是也噫道法其可偏廢乎哉誠以同其
情者先人有奪人之心善用命者然後能制人
之命如林之旅屈於一心有扈之征嚴於干紀
小惠未孚曹劌不輕於戰而亂次以濟莫敖之
敗難辭也彼恩竭而不親以道爲愚民之長物
威褻而不起以法爲繩下之彌文是自潰腹心
而故痺手足也何以立於不敗之地哉善用兵
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　二十九
punctuated: 廢，故保之如捧盈持重，人人而整齊之也。道以通其幽，恩之所以維也；法以振其顯，威之所以御也。平時鼓舞而綱紀之，固將託以生死而恃爲存亡矣。今夫同舟而濟者，百族之子，呼同聲，招同臂，率遇風波，迅以破之，而歡然利涉，其情同也。群舉以獵，獸可丘陵，而必範我馳驅，寧少而不務多者，法不可弛也。況用兵乎？今之談兵者，孰不曰察九地之利害，辯五行之生尅，明奇正之變化，覘主客之堅瑕，勵士以作其氣，用間以抒其謀，棄實以擊其虛，因形以布其勢，如是可以爲兵矣。而不知以逸待勞、以靜馭動之要，則不在是也。噫！道法其可偏廢乎哉？誠以同其情者，先人有奪人之心；善用命者，然後能制人之命。如林之旅，屈於一心；有扈之征，嚴於干紀。小惠未孚，曹劌不輕於戰；而亂次以濟，莫敖之敗難辭也。彼恩竭而不親，以道爲愚民之長物；威褻而不起，以法爲繩下之彌文，是自潰腹心而故痺手足也。何以立於不敗之地哉？善用兵
translation_en:
…fall into disuse. Thus one must preserve it as carefully as one carries a brimming vessel or bears a heavy load, bringing every man into order. The Way reaches what is hidden within: it is the means by which kindness binds men together. Law gives force to what is outwardly manifest: it is the means by which authority governs them. By inspiring them and maintaining their discipline in ordinary times, one prepares to entrust them with life and death and to depend upon them for survival or destruction.

Consider men crossing a river in the same boat. Though they come from a hundred different clans, they call out with one voice and signal with arms moving as one. Whenever wind and waves confront them, they swiftly break through and joyfully make a successful crossing, because their feelings are united. When men go out hunting together, even though game may fill the hills [?], they must keep their chariot driving within the prescribed rules. They would rather take little than strive for a large catch, because discipline must not be relaxed. How much more does this apply to warfare!

Of those who discuss warfare today, who does not say that one must examine the advantages and dangers of the nine kinds of ground, distinguish the generating and overcoming relationships of the Five Phases, understand the transformations of unorthodox and orthodox operations, and observe the strengths and weaknesses of defending and invading forces? They speak of encouraging soldiers to rouse their fighting spirit, employing spies to carry out their plans, avoiding strength to strike at weakness, and deploying strategic force according to circumstances. They think that this suffices to conduct warfare. Yet they do not understand that the essentials of awaiting an exhausted enemy at ease and controlling movement through stillness lie elsewhere.

Alas! Can either the Way or law be neglected? Those who unite men's feelings through sincerity can act before the enemy and seize his resolve; only those who know how to carry out commands can then control the lives of others. An army as dense as a forest yielded to unity of purpose; the campaign against Youhu sternly punished violations of the established order. While petty favors had not won the people's trust, Cao Gui would not lightly commit to battle. And when troops crossed in disorder, the Mo'ao could hardly escape responsibility for his defeat.

Those whose kindness is exhausted without gaining affection regard the Way as a useless accessory for deluding the people; those whose authority is treated with contempt and cannot be asserted regard law as empty elaboration for restraining their subordinates. This is to destroy one's own heart and belly and deliberately paralyze one's hands and feet. How can one thereby stand in an invincible position? Those skilled in warfare…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
者懼其胥戕也合之以油然不容已之情懼其
相伊也貞之以森然不可越之度均服食以平
其慾公喜怒以恊其衆同甘苦以馴其性念室
家以䘏其私明賞罰以釋其疑是謂脩道矣而
凡天時之陰陽寒暑地利之遠近險夷人事之
安危休戚有出於道之外者皆其所軫念焉曲
部不易其節制不爽其式偏校不迷於局轉
餉不窮於執掌管不黷於賄資用不匱於求是
謂保法矣而凡上不制於天下不制於地中不
===
制於人有出於法之外者皆其所盡心焉道之
所在如邇父母疇能忘其恩法之所在如對鬼
神疇敢玩其威故知方之民可與圖成有制之
兵可與慮敵驕虜在前勍敵在後卒然令之彼
亦毅然赴之蹈水火如坦途冐矢石如袵席其
升高也如走圓於千仞之崗其墜深也如决水
於萬丈之谿戰如雷霆摧剥而不撓攻如風雨
周旋而不逆豈其好生惡死之心與人殊哉蓋
勇生於愛愛道甚於愛身義奮於威立功先於
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　四十
punctuated: 者懼其胥戕也，合之以油然不容已之情；懼其相伊也，貞之以森然不可越之度。均服食以平其慾，公喜怒以恊其衆，同甘苦以馴其性，念室家以䘏其私，明賞罰以釋其疑，是謂脩道矣。而凡天時之陰陽寒暑，地利之遠近險夷，人事之安危休戚，有出於道之外者，皆其所軫念焉。曲部不易其節，制不爽其式，偏校不迷於局，轉餉不窮於執，掌管不黷於賄，資用不匱於求，是謂保法矣。而凡上不制於天，下不制於地，中不制於人，有出於法之外者，皆其所盡心焉。道之所在，如邇父母，疇能忘其恩？法之所在，如對鬼神，疇敢玩其威？故知方之民可與圖成，有制之兵可與慮敵。驕虜在前，勍敵在後，卒然令之，彼亦毅然赴之，蹈水火如坦途，冐矢石如袵席。其升高也，如走圓於千仞之崗；其墜深也，如决水於萬丈之谿。戰如雷霆，摧剥而不撓；攻如風雨，周旋而不逆。豈其好生惡死之心與人殊哉？蓋勇生於愛，愛道甚於愛身；義奮於威，立功先於
translation_en: …those skilled in warfare fear that their men will harm one another, and unite them through a naturally arising, irrepressible affection. Fearing that they will mutually [the wording 相伊 is unclear][?], they steady them with strict standards that cannot be transgressed. They equalize clothing and food to moderate their desires, remain impartial in pleasure and anger to harmonize the ranks, share hardship and comfort to discipline their dispositions, consider their households to show concern for their private needs, and make rewards and punishments clear to dispel their doubts. This is called cultivating the Way. Yet every matter of seasonal conditions—yin and yang, cold and heat—of terrain—distance and proximity, difficulty and ease—and of human affairs—safety and danger, happiness and distress—that falls outside the Way also receives their thoughtful attention. Units and divisions do not depart from their prescribed order; regulations do not deviate from established forms; subordinate commanders are not confused about their duties; those transporting provisions are not thwarted in carrying out their tasks; those in charge are not corrupted by bribes; and resources and supplies do not fall short of demand. This is called preserving the regulations. Yet in all matters of remaining unconstrained above by Heaven, below by Earth, and between them by other people, they also devote their full attention to whatever falls outside those regulations. Where the Way prevails, it is as though one were close to one's parents: who could forget their kindness? Where regulations prevail, it is as though one stood before ghosts and spirits: who would dare trifle with their authority? Thus, with people who understand right conduct one may plan for success; with troops governed by discipline one may deliberate on confronting the enemy. With arrogant foes ahead and powerful enemies behind, issue a sudden command and the men will resolutely hasten to obey. They tread through water and fire as though on a level road, and brave arrows and stones as though resting on bedding. Their ascent to the heights is like setting a round object rolling on a ridge a thousand ren high [?]; their descent into the depths is like releasing water into a ravine ten thousand zhang deep. In battle they are like thunder, shattering and stripping away resistance without faltering; in attack they are like wind and rain, moving in every direction without being checked. Could their love of life and aversion to death differ from those of other people? Courage arises from affection: they love the Way more than their own persons. Righteous resolve is roused by authority: establishing merit takes precedence over…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
立命人知大將之藏其用也而不知感通於無
間也人知士卒之易於使也而不知教養之有
素也以我之有餘乘敵之不足其勝不勝犁然
明矣先爲不可勝以待敵之可勝宜莫有要於
此者昔者子犯曰民未知義使之懷生民未知
信使之徵辭民未知禮使之正官申叔時曰德
以施惠刑以正邪信以守物上下和睦莫不盡
命以從上致死以補其闕蓋有以達道法之微
矣晉賴以霸而楚因之興豈偶然哉雖然旌麾
===
所指敵人開戸五十戰而不殆者不言道法者
也玄黄之實壺漿之迎農不易業市不改肆而
成戰秦陳夏之化者道法造端者也右轅左蓐
前茅慮無中權後勁百官象物而動軍政不戒
而備法勝而道微者也惠公不振旅於韓先軫
不反命於箕荀伯不復從於邲昧道而廢法者
也析爨下之骸掬舟中之指道遂而棄師居處
而求馬則道法胥淪矣豈兵家之所貴哉雖然
兵者危道聖人不得已而用之有道之可脩不
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄　四十一
punctuated:
立命。人知大將之藏其用也，而不知感通於無間也；人知士卒之易於使也，而不知教養之有素也。以我之有餘，乘敵之不足，其勝不勝，犁然明矣。先爲不可勝，以待敵之可勝，宜莫有要於此者。昔者子犯曰：「民未知義，使之懷生；民未知信，使之徵辭；民未知禮，使之正官。」申叔時曰：「德以施惠，刑以正邪，信以守物，上下和睦，莫不盡命以從上，致死以補其闕。」蓋有以達道法之微矣。晉賴以霸，而楚因之興，豈偶然哉？

雖然，旌麾所指，敵人開戸，五十戰而不殆者，不言道法者也。玄黄之實，壺漿之迎，農不易業，市不改肆，而成戰秦陳夏之化者，道法造端者也。右轅左蓐，前茅慮無，中權後勁，百官象物而動，軍政不戒而備，法勝而道微者也。惠公不振旅於韓，先軫不反命於箕，荀伯不復從於邲，昧道而廢法者也。析爨下之骸，掬舟中之指，道遂而棄師，居處而求馬，則道法胥淪矣，豈兵家之所貴哉？

雖然，兵者危道，聖人不得已而用之。有道之可脩，不
translation_en:
…preserving their own lives. People know that a great general keeps his methods concealed, but do not know that an unbroken sympathetic bond connects him with his men. People know that soldiers are easy to command, but do not know that they have long been instructed and nurtured. When we use our abundance to exploit the enemy’s deficiencies, whether we shall prevail becomes perfectly clear. First make oneself invincible, then await an opportunity to defeat the enemy: surely nothing is more essential than this. Formerly, Zifan said: “The people did not yet understand righteousness, so he caused them to cherish life; they did not yet understand trustworthiness, so he caused them to substantiate their statements; they did not yet understand ritual propriety, so he caused them to set official ranks in order.” Shen Shushi said: “Use virtue to bestow benefits, punishments to correct wrongdoing, and trustworthiness to maintain affairs. When superiors and inferiors live in harmony, all will devote their lives to following their superiors and risk death to remedy their shortcomings.” These men surely grasped the subtleties of the Way and military regulation. Jin relied on these to attain hegemony, and Chu rose through them. Could this have been accidental?

Yet those whose banners point the way and whose enemies open their gates, who fight fifty battles without peril, are those who do not speak of the Way and regulation. Those who receive gifts of dark and yellow silk [?] and are welcomed with pitchers of drink, under whom farmers continue their occupations and markets retain their shops, and who accomplish the transforming influence described as “fighting Qin and arraying Xia” [?], are those who establish the beginnings of the Way and regulation. With chariots on the right and foragers on the left, scouts ahead guarding against unforeseen dangers, command in the center, and strong troops in the rear, the hundred officers act according to their designated emblems, and military arrangements are complete without admonition: here regulation predominates while the Way is weak. Duke Hui failed to bring his troops home from Han; Xian Zhen failed to return and report his mission from Ji; and Xun Bo was no longer obeyed at Bi. These were cases of obscuring the Way and abandoning regulation. When bones are split for fuel beneath cooking pots and severed fingers are scooped up from boats, when “the way proceeds and the army is abandoned” [?], and horses are sought in dwellings [?], then both the Way and regulation have sunk into oblivion. How could military thinkers esteem such things?

Nevertheless, warfare is a perilous course; sages employ it only when they have no alternative. To have a Way that can be cultivated does not…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
若相忘於道有法之可保不若無事於法蓋至
愛無恩而天下泯其愛至畏無威而天下泯其
畏何者以天而勝人也孫武之言雖若近理然
執此以爲勝人之要是其心未嘗一日不在功
利茍不能勝雖兵連禍結殺人盈野未厭足也
後之好大喜功者其十三篇爲之作俑歟故曰
孫子之道法不如三代之仁義三代之仁義不
如邃古之無爲
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄 四十二
punctuated: 若相忘於道。有法之可保，不若無事於法。蓋至愛無恩，而天下泯其愛；至畏無威，而天下泯其畏。何者？以天而勝人也。孫武之言雖若近理，然執此以爲勝人之要，是其心未嘗一日不在功利。茍不能勝，雖兵連禍結，殺人盈野，未厭足也。後之好大喜功者，其十三篇爲之作俑歟？故曰：孫子之道法不如三代之仁義，三代之仁義不如邃古之無爲。
translation_en: …is not as good as forgetting one another in the Way. Having military methods that can be maintained is not as good as having no occasion to employ them. For the utmost love bestows no favors, and all under Heaven cease to be conscious of that love; the utmost awe displays no might, and all under Heaven cease to be conscious of that awe. Why is this? Because it is through Heaven that one prevails over men. Although Sun Wu’s words seem close to the truth, to seize upon them as the key to overcoming others means that one’s mind is never, for even a single day, free from thoughts of achievement and gain. If victory cannot be attained, even unending warfare, accumulating calamities, and fields filled with the slain will not satisfy such ambition. Was it not his Thirteen Chapters that set the precedent for those in later ages who craved grandeur and delighted in feats of conquest? Thus I say: Sunzi’s Way and military methods are inferior to the benevolence and righteousness of the Three Dynasties; the benevolence and righteousness of the Three Dynasties are inferior to the nonaction of remote antiquity.

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
福建武舉錄後序
乙卯秋閩屬大比文士之期
巡按御史胡〔志夔〕監臨其事
維明維公得人爲盛冬十月
爰飭舊章再典武試綜理惕
慎不減於文焉於是諸鈐武
弁之流八郡良家之子畢集
===
而胥校之亦旣汰之維精群
無留良矣行將造之大司馬
以考成功謂非一鄉之盛事
哉錄成御史命廷誥序之末
簡迺作而言曰天下之材由
養而成由振起而後盛非偶
然也文王綱紀四方勉勉不
banxin: 武舉御試錄後序 一
punctuated:
福建武舉錄後序

乙卯秋，閩屬大比文士之期，巡按御史胡〔志夔〕監臨其事，維明維公，得人爲盛。冬十月，爰飭舊章，再典武試，綜理惕慎，不減於文焉。於是諸鈐武弁之流、八郡良家之子畢集，而胥校之，亦旣汰之維精，群無留良矣。行將造之大司馬，以考成功，謂非一鄉之盛事哉？錄成，御史命廷誥序之末簡，迺作而言曰：天下之材，由養而成，由振起而後盛，非偶然也。文王綱紀四方，勉勉不
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Military Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the yimao year [1555], Fujian reached the season for the triennial examination of civil candidates. Regional Inspector Hu〔Zhikui〕supervised the proceedings. Discerning and impartial, he achieved distinction through the recruitment of worthy men. In winter, in the tenth month, he duly enforced the established regulations and once again presided over the military examination, managing its affairs with vigilance and care no less than he had devoted to the civil examination. Military commanders and officers [?], together with sons of respectable families from the eight prefectures, all assembled and were examined together. After elimination had refined the selection to the best, no worthy man among them remained overlooked. They would shortly be sent to the Minister of War for assessment of their attainments. Could this be called anything other than a splendid event for the province?

When the record was completed, the Regional Inspector instructed me, Tinggao, to write a postface on its final leaves. I therefore rose and said: Talent in the world develops through cultivation and flourishes only after it has been stirred into activity; this does not happen by chance. King Wen ordered the four quarters, diligently and without…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
倦故髦士六師後先輩出以
之折衝禦侮克咸厥勳雖罝
兎武夫赳赳爭雄足稱干城
腹心之器何者機之所使上
感而下應也我
國家定鼎開基垂二百年文武
並庸熙洽長久至其流也儒
===
術耻言兵華世官狎於輕肥
文浸盛而武日slt以衰橫虜
猾疆淫寇窺圉需用甚急蓋
未聞有縱艫鯨鼇鳴劍龍庭
少紓華夏之氣者豈下之無
其人歟仰惟
皇上赫然啓圖懋昭
banxin: 武舉鄉試録後序 二
punctuated:
倦，故髦士六師後先輩出，以之折衝禦侮，克咸厥勳。雖罝兎武夫，赳赳爭雄，足稱干城腹心之器。何者？機之所使，上感而下應也。
我國家定鼎開基，垂二百年，文武並庸，熙洽長久。至其流也，儒術耻言兵，華世官狎於輕肥，文浸盛而武日slt以衰。橫虜猾疆，淫寇窺圉，需用甚急。蓋未聞有縱艫鯨鼇、鳴劍龍庭，少紓華夏之氣者，豈下之無其人歟？仰惟皇上赫然啓圖，懋昭
translation_en:
…untiring. Thus outstanding men and warriors of the Six Armies emerged in succession; through them, enemy attacks were repelled and insults resisted, and their achievements were brought to completion. Even rabbit-netting warriors, martial and vying in valor, were worthy to serve as shields and walls and as trusted intimates. Why was this? Such was the working of the animating impulse: influence from above elicited a response below.
Our dynasty established its capital and laid its foundations nearly two hundred years ago. Civil and military talents were employed together, and harmony and prosperity long endured. As this legacy degenerated, however, scholars versed in Confucian learning became ashamed to discuss warfare, while illustrious hereditary officials [?] grew accustomed to light fur robes and well-fed horses. Civil pursuits gradually flourished, while military affairs declined day by day [the transcription contains the corrupt text “slt”]. Violent northern foes disturbed the frontiers, and rapacious raiders eyed our borders; the need for military talent became urgent. Yet we have heard of none who launched warships against the great whales and turtles, or made swords ring at the Dragon Court of the northern foes, thereby bringing some relief to the pent-up spirit of the Chinese realm. Can it be that there are no such men among those below?
We reverently consider how His Majesty has magnificently inaugurated his plans and splendidly manifested…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
聖武
躬臨大閱復舉制科精神氣象視
周彌光焉故邊臣場吏罔不
奮迅尤
拊髀興思欲網羅一二名將以
分樹南北之衝適觀安攘之
績廣宸
===
廷議敷之
明詔傳布寰宇豐爵賞以激其志
運鼓舞以和其衷旁招側陋
之濵博採沉淪之地固有以
回易視聽而奔走英雄矣非
有機以使之者耶御史恭承
德意夙夜劬勞澄鑑懸衡丕釐積
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄後序 三
punctuated: 聖武，躬臨大閱，復舉制科，精神氣象視周彌光焉。故邊臣場吏罔不奮迅，尤拊髀興思，欲網羅一二名將，以分樹南北之衝，適觀安攘之績。廣宸廷議，敷之明詔，傳布寰宇，豐爵賞以激其志，運鼓舞以和其衷，旁招側陋之濵，博採沉淪之地，固有以回易視聽而奔走英雄矣。非有機以使之者耶？御史恭承德意，夙夜劬勞，澄鑑懸衡，丕釐積
translation_en:
…sagely martial prowess. He personally attended the grand military review and revived the special examination. In spirit and bearing, his reign shines yet more brilliantly than the Zhou. Thus frontier officials and examination-ground functionaries all sprang into action. Above all, His Majesty slapped his thigh in eager contemplation, wishing to recruit one or two renowned generals and station them at strategic points in the south and north, there to witness their achievements in securing peace and repelling aggression. Deliberations at the imperial court were broadened [?] and set forth in an enlightened edict, promulgated throughout the realm. Generous ranks and rewards stirred their aspirations; encouragement brought their hearts into accord. Men were summoned from obscure and humble places, and talent was sought widely among those languishing unrecognized. These measures could indeed transform what people saw and heard and bring heroes hastening into service. Was there not a means by which they were moved to act?

The censor reverently received the imperial intention and labored day and night, keeping his discerning mirror clear and his scales suspended, thoroughly rectifying accumulated …

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
盡辯藝於射考猷於文式者
上不式者下期獲全材以酬
廟堂宵旰之求僅僅得若干人
焉諸士之與茲選亦惟難矣
不足爲榮哉夫藝其習也今
程之能矣猷其蘊也今奏之
言矣能之必可成言之必可
===
行三代之將所爲全材也顧
非當自期待者歟邇者海酋
之毒滋於下土諸士翺翔國
族目炙時虜讐之見傷於虎
談之而有不色變者乎色變
矣有不思寢處其皮者乎矧
諸士培養於
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄後序　四
punctuated:
盡，辯藝於射，考猷於文，式者上，不式者下，期獲全材以酬廟堂宵旰之求，僅僅得若干人焉。諸士之與茲選，亦惟難矣，不足爲榮哉？夫藝其習也，今程之能矣；猷其蘊也，今奏之言矣。能之必可成，言之必可行，三代之將所爲全材也，顧非當自期待者歟？
邇者海酋之毒滋於下土，諸士翺翔國族，目炙時虜讐之見傷於虎，談之而有不色變者乎？色變矣，有不思寢處其皮者乎？矧諸士培養於
translation_en:
…to the utmost. Skill was distinguished through archery, and strategic judgment assessed through written compositions. Those meeting the standard were ranked above, and those failing it below. The aim was to obtain men of all-round ability to answer the court’s quest, pursued from early morning until late at night; yet only a handful were found. For you gentlemen to have gained this selection was indeed difficult. Is this not sufficient cause for pride? Skill is what you have practiced, and your proficiency has now been tested; strategic judgment is what you hold within, and you have now presented it in words. What you are capable of must assuredly be accomplished, and what you say must assuredly be put into practice. This is what constituted all-round ability in the generals of the Three Dynasties. Should you not hold yourselves to that expectation?
Recently, the scourge of maritime chieftains has spread through the land. You gentlemen move among the people of the realm [?] and have witnessed the injuries inflicted by these enemies, savage as tigers [?]. Can anyone speak of this without changing color? Having changed color, could anyone fail to wish to sleep upon their flayed skins? How much more so for you gentlemen, who have been nurtured under…

title: 嘉靖三十四年福建武舉鄉試錄
text:
聖明之朝周旋於賓興之典則靖
獻有階矣展奇謀以挫敵鋒
輸死力以雪國耻當不俟驅
策而奮勇先登者夫名浮於
實謂之虛聲功不與時偕謂
之悻機是徒侈其榮而不念
其難者也豈上之人求材之
意哉先是翳陰彌空浹旬不
===
開初試之晨倏爾日麗旌麾
炳彩山川耀靈介胄若不可
犯御史喜曰茲海嶽清明妖
氛其蕩滌乎馳馬甫閑束矢
其橐雲升雨施既霑既濡纖
塵不動御史又喜曰茲時雨
banxin: 武舉鄉試錄後序　五
punctuated:
聖明之朝，周旋於賓興之典，則靖獻有階矣。展奇謀以挫敵鋒，輸死力以雪國耻，當不俟驅策而奮勇先登者。夫名浮於實，謂之虛聲；功不與時偕，謂之悻機。是徒侈其榮而不念其難者也，豈上之人求材之意哉？
先是，翳陰彌空，浹旬不開。初試之晨，倏爾日麗，旌麾炳彩，山川耀靈，介胄若不可犯。御史喜曰：「茲海嶽清明，妖氛其蕩滌乎！」馳馬甫閑，束矢其橐，雲升雨施，既霑既濡，纖塵不動。御史又喜曰：「茲時雨
translation_en:
…in the court of a sage and enlightened ruler, and participating in the ceremonial selection of worthy men, you now have a means of offering loyal service. You should devise extraordinary stratagems to blunt the enemy’s advance and exert yourselves to the death to wipe away the state’s humiliation, courageously striving to be first into the fray without waiting to be urged onward. When reputation exceeds substance, it is called empty fame; when achievement fails to keep pace with the times, it is called grasping at opportunity [?]. Such men merely vaunt their glory without considering the difficulties involved. Could this be what those above intend in seeking talent?
Before this, dark clouds had filled the sky for ten days without clearing. On the morning of the first test, the sun suddenly shone brightly. Banners and standards gleamed with color; mountains and rivers shone with spiritual radiance; the armored men seemed invincible.
